messages.content: 在DMO模式下，呼叫优先级的等级排列顺序是怎样的？高优先级呼叫如何处理低优先级呼叫占用的信道资源？
DMO模式下的呼叫优先级由低到高依次为普通优先级、高优先级、预占优先级。当低优先级呼叫占用信道资源时，高优先级呼叫可打断低优先级呼叫，以获得信道资源。
终端发起个呼或组呼时，若将呼叫优先级设置为“未定义”，系统将如何确定实际使用的优先级？
若设置为“未定义”，则以系统为终端设置的呼叫优先级为准。
在个呼和组呼的优先级设置中，“优先级1-11”与“预占优先级1-3”在功能上有什么主要区别？
“优先级1-11”不具有预占功能；而“预占优先级1-3”具有预占功能，可打断优先级低的呼叫。
开启“广播呼叫优先”功能后，终端接入广播组呼的行为会发生什么变化？如果不开启该功能，系统将依据什么来接入广播呼叫？
开启后，终端将优先接入其他终端或调度台发起的广播组呼，以保证接入更及时。如果不开启，系统将根据“使用等级”来接入广播呼叫。
配置通话组频率时有什么要求？
需设置在终端支持的频率范围内。
开启“手动切换优先”功能后，终端在什么情况下才会选择其他符合条件的邻站进行登记？
只有当该基站失锁（即终端无法接收基站的信号）时，终端才会根据扫描策略去选择其他符合条件的邻站进行登记。
输入系统码切换基站时，对目标基站系统码与输入系统码的一致性有何具体要求？如果不满足会怎样？
目标基站系统码与输入的系统码必须相同（对比前14bit）才允许登记；否则，作为干扰信道丢弃。
当手动切换优先功能开启且手动切换基站成功时，终端会对扫描策略和自动优选基站功能执行什么操作？
终端将关闭扫描策略（无论该扫描功能是否开启），并关闭自动优选基站功能（无论该功能是否开启）。
在“信道信息”菜单中，系统码是如何获取和显示的？越区切换后有何变化？
系统码为系统广播而非终端配置，取前14bit十进制显示。越区切换后显示新站系统码。
在“信道信息”菜单中，基站别名和基站编号的显示需要满足哪些匹配条件？
仅当登记站与信道列表中基站匹配上，且该基站有设置时才显示。匹配规则为：登记站与信道列表中某一个基站的系统码和信道号都相同；若基站未配置系统码，则只对比信道号。
控制信道计划为固定或灵活时，扫描模式菜单的显示和编辑状态有何不同？
当控制信道计划为固定控制信道时，扫描模式菜单显示并可编辑；当控制信道计划为灵活控制信道时，扫描模式菜单隐藏。
Which audio accessory is identified as a Wireless PTT?
The POA121 is the Wireless PTT audio accessory.
What are the two types of NB mode and how do they differ in operation?

The two types are Direct mode operation (DMO) and Trunking mode operation (TMO). DMO supports only simplex operation and communicates directly on a fixed channel frequency or through repeaters. TMO supports either duplex or simplex operation and communicates on the channel frequency allocated by the trunking system.
What does it indicate when the LED indicator flashes orange?
It indicates that the radio is registering in TMO, or establishing a call with hook signaling in TMO (applicable only to the called radio).
How do you switch between DMO and TMO modes?
Press Settings > PMP > Operating Mode, and then press DMO or TMO.
IP的英文全称和中文全称分别是什么？
IP的英文全称是Internet Protocol，中文全称是互联网协议。
G2集群终端数据透传功能的主要目的是什么？
为G2集群终端提供数据透传功能，同时兼容G1车台和G1终端的数据透传功能。
在集群窄带网络的数据透传模式中，设备对用户数据的具体处理方式是什么？
设备（包括支持数据透传的G2终端、G1终端和车台）只负责将用户数据完整地传输到目的节点，不对用户数据进行解析。用户数据的封装和解析完全由用户端的业务进行处理。
利用集群窄带网络实现透明传输通道对基于串口开发的用户设备程序有何优势？
这使得已经基于串口开发的用户设备程序能够不经任何调整地使用现有的NB通路，无需进行额外的二次开发即可传输自定义的通信协议。
当外部设备将数据传递给车台时，数据在传输过程中会发生什么变化？
这组数据不发生任何形式的改变，并通过空口协议进行传输，车台将数据原封不动地传输到最终接收者手里。
什么是空口通路？
空口通路是指NB与NB之间的空口通信。
NB如何通过空口通路与基站进行通信？
NB通过空口通路5与基站进行通信，并将数据透传给基站。
在网关通路中，基站如何处理数据？
基站将数据透传给专用网关。
目前数据透传提供哪两种可选方式？
目前有两种方式可供选择：A. 自适应；B. 仅使用分组数据传输（专有型或共享型）。
在CPS或MDM上配置传输方式时，目前有哪些选项可供选择？
目前有两种方式可供选择：A. 自适应；B. 仅使用分组数据传输（专有型或共享型）。
空口通路采用哪些方式进行传输，其重发策略如何确定？
空口通路采用短消息或者分组数据进行传输，其空口的重发策略与短消息或者分组数据相同。
在自适应模式下，NB 如何决定数据传输方式？
NB 自动判断使用短数据还是分组数据进行传输。
How do you add a Conventional AIE key for DMR?
Enter the key name, set Type as DMR, set Key Type as AIE, set Model, and then click OK. Then click New, and configure the key length and value.
What are the settings required to configure conventional or trunking E2EE keys in DMR?
Enter the key name, set Type as DMR, set Key Type as E2EE, set Work Mode as Trunking or Conventional/XPT accordingly, and then click OK.
What is the full name of the abbreviation AIE?
AIE stands for Air Interface Encryption.
What are the supported frequency bands for TETRA wireless data communication?
TETRA supports the frequency bands 350-470MHz and 806-870MHz.
What distinguishes Hytera HyTalk MC from Hytera HyTalk Pro when integrated with the PTC760?

Hytera HyTalk MC is a PMR characterized talk solution deployed over public networks providing stable PTT communication, high-speed data applications, and multimedia services. Hytera HyTalk Pro provides high-quality audio and video services along with instant messaging.
How do you operate the Smart Knob on the PDM680 to adjust volume versus select a channel?
To adjust the volume, rotate the Smart Knob. To select a channel, press the knob and then rotate it.
What is the correct orientation for inserting Micro SD cards into the slots?
Insert the Micro SD cards with the metal contacts facing down.
什么是中继模式？
中继模式是指终端作为网关，将接收到的专网语音或公网语音在专网和公网之间相互转发。
使用中继模式有什么前提条件？
该模式需授权后才可使用。
在中继模式下，终端屏幕如何显示网络状态？
终端屏幕上半部分显示公网状态界面，下半部分显示专网状态界面。
在中继模式下，如何切换并识别当前所选的界面？
可以通过按【上移】/【下移】方向键选择专网状态界面或公网状态界面，界面左侧显示标志的为当前所选界面。
在中继模式下的专网待机界面，能否通过按【上移】/【下移】方向键选择区域？
不能。在中继模式下的专网待机界面，不能通过按【上移】/【下移】方向键选择区域。
当设备显示PI或PE图标时，分别表示扫描停留在哪个信道？
PI表示扫描停留于优先信道1，PE表示扫描停留于优先信道2。
如何设置待机状态下当前信道在屏幕上的显示方式？支持哪些显示选项？
选择“设置 > 对讲机偏好设置 > 信道显示模式”菜单进行设置。支持的显示方式为信道号、别名或频率。
如何配置设备启动紧急报警的信道？
通过“报警跳转信道”设置设备启动紧急报警的信道。
开启“自动紧急呼叫”后，设备在紧急呼叫模式下有何表现？
设备紧急呼叫模式下会自动打开麦克风，用户无需按PTT即可发射语音。
Which technology is referred to by the abbreviation DMR?
DMR refers to Digital Mobile Radio.
PDT refers to which communication system?
PDT refers to Police Digital Trunking.
What is the intended purpose of this ETSI Technical Report (ETR) regarding TETRA solutions?
It is intended to serve as an informative reference document for network operators or managers of mobile radio systems who are contemplating TErrestrial Trunked RAdio (TETRA) solutions.
What is the definition of a Base Station (BS) in the context of TETRA network requirements?

A Base Station (BS) is a physical grouping of equipment that provides the fixed portion of the air interface. One BS transmits and receives radio signals to and from a single location area, which is a single region of geographical coverage.
What specific information is contained in a subscriber activity log?

A subscriber activity log contains information on attach/detach Individual TETRA Subscriber Identity (ITSI); enable/disable terminal; registrations; location updates vs. time; call re-establishment; authentication; call start time, call end time, and called party; type of call; supplementary services invoked; whether uplink Bit Error Ratio (BER) or Message Error Rate (MER) are below an operator pre-determined threshold; plus any other relevant activity record.
What are the only two types of subscriber terminals defined in the text?
The only types of subscriber terminal are Mobile Stations (MS) and Line Stations (LS).
What components constitute the Switching and Management Infrastructure (SwMI) in a TETRA Voice plus Data network?
The SwMI consists of all TETRA equipment for a Voice plus Data (V+D) network except for subscriber terminals.
What are the typical standardized central network management functions for TETRA networks?

Typical standardized central network management functions include: temporary withdrawal and restoration of registration permission; subscriber activity history and current status; initiating trace of future subscriber activities; performance management (data transfer from LNM to CNM); fault or maintenance management (alarms for serious equipment failure, security breach, or traffic alarm); accounting management (data transfer for users with wide roaming capability); and security procedures (authentication and authorization).
Why do certain aspects of TETRA network management not need to be standardized across networks?
Certain aspects do not need to be standardized because they are performed only within a single TETRA network at a local level.
How is a single tier TETRA system typically structured in terms of network components and management?

A single tier TETRA system, often used for small compact networks, comprises a number of base stations inter-connected by some form of network. A Network Management Facility (NMF) is attached to this network, from which all necessary management functions can be exercised.
What are the possible configurations for operators and terminals in a single tier TETRA system?

The management facility may be a single terminal used by a single operator who performs all network management functions. Alternatively, for a slightly larger system, it may involve more than one network operator, each with different permitted roles, potentially using more than one terminal. Different operators, service providers, users, or managers may handle different sets of functions, such as subscriber and security management, network configuration, fault management, and performance management.
What are the primary responsibilities of regional network management facilities in a large TETRA system?

Regional network management facilities typically control their own network configuration and fault management, subject to existing network management policies. They may also send faults deemed of sufficient severity to the central network manager.
How is a TETRA system supplied by multiple manufacturers structured in terms of independence and management?

A multi-supplier TETRA system is viewed as comprising several tiers and branches, where each branch can be largely independent. Each supplier's system operates as a separate network with its own local network management facility.
What is the purpose of Clause 7 regarding NMFs for TETRA systems?
Clause 7 assists end user organizations in writing organization-specific functional requirements specifications for NMFs for TETRA systems, using ETR 292 [1] as a guideline.
What should be clarified before writing a detailed functional specification for TETRA infrastructure?
It should be clear in what way the TETRA infrastructure will be managed, specifically how the management will be organized.
Does the distinction between central and local management imply that the infrastructure consists of multiple TETRA networks?
No, the central and local management mentioned do not imply that the infrastructure consists of multiple TETRA networks.
How does end user organization change impact the flexibility requirements of a TETRA network management system?

The system must address whether the end user organization is likely to change during the network's lifetime and determine the impact on network management organization, including identifying facilities needed to anticipate expected changes such as support for change management.
Which document clauses introduce the subject of TETRA network management standardization?
Clauses 1 to 4 of ETR 292 [1] introduce the subject of TETRA network management standardization.
What is the first step an end user organization should take when writing functional requirements specifications for TETRA system management using ETR 292 as a guideline?
The first step is to decide how the Network Management will be organized.
In the process of writing functional requirements for TETRA management, what factors must be considered when deciding whether a specific management function is required?
When deciding whether a management function is required, the conditions formulated in the steps regarding organization, locations, players/tasks, and system flexibility must be taken into account.
What is the final step listed in the procedure for writing functional requirements specifications for TETRA system management?
The final step is to consider on which geographic locations the management function should be available.
Which RFC defines the convention for describing SNMP Agents?
RFC 1303 defines the convention for describing SNMP Agents.
What is the title of RFC 1442 in the context of SNMP v2?
The title of RFC 1442 is Structure of Management Information for SNMP v2.
Which RFC addresses the coexistence between SNMP v1 and SNMP v2?
RFC 1452 addresses the coexistence between SNMP v1 and SNMP v2.
海能达PTC680对讲机在哪些状态下不会产生射频能量辐射？
接收（收听）和待机时均不会产生射频能量辐射，仅在发射（讲话）时产生。
USB连接电脑时，选择“不进行数据传输”模式有什么作用？
设备仅与电脑连接，电脑无法读取数据，但可以为设备读写频。
什么是己方组文件夹（己方夹），它有什么数量限制？
己方组文件夹简称己方夹，即默认组所在的文件夹。您可以把需要发起语音呼叫或短消息的组添加到该文件夹中，己方夹有且只能有一个。
HOOK 呼叫和 DIRECT 呼叫的接听方式有何不同？
HOOK 呼叫有振铃提示，需在预设时间内按【PTT】键接听；DIRECT 呼叫自动建立，无需任何操作即可接听。
接收到 PSTN/PABX 呼叫后如何接听？
按【返回/接听】键或按【PTT】键接听该呼叫。
直通模式和集群模式都支持的最大发射功率有哪些？
直通模式和集群模式都支持的最大发射功率为 1.8 W (32.5 dBm)、1 W (30 dBm) 和 0.56 W (27.5 dBm)。
集群模式和直通模式下的紧急报警模式有何区别？紧急静默模式的特征是什么？
集群模式下，紧急报警模式分为紧急模式和紧急静默模式；直通模式下，只有紧急模式。紧急静默模式的特征是：对讲机发起紧急呼叫时，无任何界面、LED 灯或提示音等。
在紧急报警时，如果发起方未按【PTT】键释放话语权，接收方会有什么限制？如何解决？
接收方将不能申请话语权。为了避免这一情况，可以配置开启紧急轮询功能，让呼叫双方轮流获得话语权进行对讲。
在对讲机直通模式下，如果选择的工作方式为中继、网关或中继和网关，需要进行什么额外操作？
需开启自动选择设备或手动添加设备。
对讲机在直通模式和集群模式下通信的基本要求或脱网处理机制分别是什么？
直通模式要求对讲机必须在同一个网络中才能进行通信。集群模式下，若信号变弱或移出覆盖范围导致脱网，需切换到其他可用网络并注册成功后方可继续通信；若配置了自动切换网络，脱网后会自动切换并注册到可用网络。
在集群模式下，PSTN网关和PABX网关的默认地址分别是多少？如何手动选择或设置网关？
PSTN网关地址默认为16777184，PABX网关地址默认为16777186。若配置了多个网关地址，可手动选择呼叫网关和信息网关。设置方法为：点击“对讲设置”，选择“PSTN网关”或“PABX网关”进行设置。
什么是集群模式下的固定小区？配置固定小区应用后，切换文件夹时会发生什么？
固定小区是指文件夹关联到指定小区，一个小区允许关联多个文件夹，以确保参与呼叫的对讲机能快速注册到指定小区并充分利用信道资源。若配置了固定小区应用，切换文件夹时，对讲机会注册到与该文件夹关联的小区。
在集群模式下，若对讲机配置了 GSDM 功能，当处于信号较弱且无可用小区的环境时，支持哪些通信操作？
支持接收组呼、发起或接收紧急呼叫、发送或接收紧急状态消息。
集群模式下对讲机进入节能模式需要满足哪些条件，其工作原理是什么？
进入节能模式前需向基站请求，只有在基站支持节能并接受请求时，对讲机才能进入。进入后，在无语音数据业务时，对讲机将定期接收基站下发的数据，以减少控制信道繁忙，达到节能目的。
集群模式下的组呼探测功能是如何实现的？
组呼探测通过状态消息实现带确认组呼。调度台发起组呼并建立成功后，向参与对讲机发送指定状态消息；对讲机收到后自动回复指定状态消息；调度台根据收到的回复统计参与数量。该功能在呼叫结束时退出。
FOACSU 和 OACSU 在中文全称上有什么区别？
FOACSU 的中文全称是手动摘机呼叫，OACSU 的中文全称是自动摘机呼叫。
当USB配置为“不进行数据传输”时，设备与电脑连接有什么特点？
电脑无法读取数据，但可以为设备读写频。
如何新建一个扫描列表？
点击 + ，选择 “新建扫描列表” 并输入扫描列表名称。
如何将扫描列表的快捷方式发送到桌面？
长按扫描列表并选择 “发送桌面快捷方式”，扫描列表的快捷方式将会出现在应用中心。
HOOK 呼叫和 DIRECT 呼叫的接听方式分别是什么？
HOOK 呼叫：对讲机有来电振铃提示，在预设时间内按【PTT】键接听该呼叫。DIRECT 呼叫：自动建立呼叫，无需任何操作即可接听。
声控功能适用于什么场景，且当前仅支持通过何种配件触发？
声控功能适用于用户双手无空暇的情况，可通过语音直接发起窄带呼叫。当前对讲机仅支持通过耳塞式配件来触发声控。
在紧急报警时，如果发起方未按【PTT】键释放话语权，接收方会遇到什么问题？如何解决？
接收方将不能申请话语权。为了避免这一情况，可以配置开启紧急轮询功能，让呼叫双方轮流获得话语权进行对讲。
在集群模式下，若对讲机配置了自动切换网络功能，脱网后会发生什么？
脱网后会自动切换并注册到可用网络。
集群模式下 PSTN 网关和 PABX 网关的默认地址分别是多少？
PSTN 网关地址默认为 16777184，PABX 网关地址默认为 16777186。
在集群模式下，对讲机配置了 GSDM 功能后，在信号较弱且无可用小区时支持哪些操作？
可以接收组呼、发起或接收紧急呼叫、发送或接收紧急状态消息等。
集群模式下对讲机进入节能模式需要满足什么条件，其工作原理是什么？
进入节能模式前需向基站请求，只有在基站支持节能并接受请求时，对讲机才能进入。进入后，在无语音数据业务时，对讲机将定期接收基站下发的数据，以减少控制信道繁忙，达到节能目的。
FOACSU和OACSU分别代表什么中文含义？
FOACSU代表手动摘机呼叫，OACSU代表自动摘机呼叫。
FLEX编码格式支持哪三种信号速率？
ERMES系统的工作频带和信道配置是怎样的？
该系统在169.4-169.8 MHz频带中的16个邻接的25 kHz信道中的一个或多个信道上工作。
InFLEXion协议在数据速率超过100 kbit/s的情况下支持哪些增值数据业务？
InFLEXion协议使在全球寻呼市场中能够重新出现语音寻呼以及增值数据业务，诸如无线传真、图像和多媒体应用。
为什么话音传信可以达到与语言无关？
因为该消息从呼叫方向用户传送，所以不需要翻译。
IDRA系统的工作频带是多少？
IDRA工作在850-915 MHz和1 453-1 525 MHz频带。
Project 25系统目前工作在哪些频带，主要用于什么领域？
Project 25系统正在VHF、UHF和800 MHz频带中工作，用于公共安全通信。
FCC在2000年的频谱分配方案中，对美国公共安全用的700 MHz频带规定了多大的带宽？
24 MHz带宽。
TETRAPOL选择FDMA和GMSK调制的主要属性针对的是哪个市场？
专业用户市场。
TETRAPOL的安全机制设计有何特点？
从一开始就已经将安全机制设计到协议中去，以便得到高水平的安全性能的同时，对性能没有影响。
在CDMA-PAMR系统中，一个载波最多可以支持多少个语音用户？
一个CDMA-PAMR载波可以最多支持35个语音用户。
FLEX的多速率性能是如何实现的？
FLEX的多速率性能是通过将一个、二个或四个1 600 bit/s业务信道复用在一起实现的。
在ERMES系统中，PNC的主要功能是什么？
PNC是网络的中心呼叫处理单元，负责呼叫处理。为了保证服务质量，PNC对每一次呼叫尝试从呼叫认可机制着手，并与发出状态信息的操作和维护中心（OMC）协作。此外，PNC通过I6接口处理用户对话以接入业务。
在提供漫游服务的网络中，对16信道中的公共信道有什么要求？
在提供漫游服务的网络中，16信道中应该至少有一个信道是公共的。在每一网络中，公共信道不一定是相同的。
该传输协议的符号率和比特率分别是多少？
符号率为3.125 kBd，比特率为6.25 kbit/s。
ERMES系统在工作频率和网络架构方面有哪些主要技术特征？
ERMES在一个射频频带中使用16个频率中的一个或多个进行工作，确保接收机在任何传输频率下都能接收到呼叫，并支持同时发射的环境。它能够用频分和时分的网络以及联播发射进行工作。
ERMES提供了哪些基本寻呼功能和高级服务？
ERMES提供的基本寻呼功能包括单音、数字和文字服务。它还可以提供高级服务，如非格式化的数据传输、靠近的用户群呼、长消息、优先级、安全设备和漫游等。
在 Hytera 手册中，符号【】代表什么意义？
该符号表示硬件界面控件名称，例如：按【PTT】键。
使用【智能】旋钮切换信道或联系人时，如何返回音量调节状态？
如果5秒内未操作或在5秒内再次按下【智能】旋钮，将返回音量调节状态。
对讲机的越区切换功能是如何工作的？
在呼叫过程中，若因位置变化导致接收的基站信号变差从而影响通话质量，对讲机会自动登记到信号更好的基站上，以保障通话不间断。
如何查看对讲机的专网号码和频率范围等信息？
点击“对讲设置”，选择“对讲机信息”，即可查看对讲机的专网号码、频率范围等信息。
如何通过对讲机的通讯录发起组呼？
点击“对讲联系人”或“对讲机”，点击“通讯录”，选择“组呼”列表中的联系人，按住【PTT】键发起组呼；或者打开组呼联系人详情界面，点击发起组呼。
在常规模式下使用一键呼叫功能发起组呼时，需要执行哪些按键操作？
需在按【一键呼叫/消息】快捷键后再按【PTT】键发起呼叫。
在模拟信道上如何发起呼叫以及对方如何接听？
按下并旋转【智能】旋钮选择所需发起呼叫的模拟信道，按住【PTT】键发起呼叫。在当前模拟信道上的对讲机检测到匹配信号后，无需任何操作即可接听。
什么是超时禁发功能，触发后如何处理？
超时禁发是指个呼、组呼或全呼时按住【PTT】键的持续时间超过预设单次发射时间（默认为 60 秒），对讲机将自动终止发射并发出警告音。松开【PTT】键可以停止警告音。如需再次通话，请在预设时间后再次按住【PTT】键发射。此功能默认开启。
如何设置对讲机以自动对组呼通话中每个成员的讲话进行录音？
点击“对讲设置”，点击“会话式录音”，开启后自动对组呼通话中每个成员的讲话进行录音。
对讲机的控制信道扫描分为哪两种类型，各自适用于什么场景？
控制信道扫描分为固定扫描和灵活扫描。当对讲机频谱资源的收发频率间隔为固定值时，采用固定控制信道扫描；当对讲机频率无规律时，采用灵活控制信道扫描。
在常规模式下，如何手动发起远程监听？
点击“对讲联系人”或“对讲机”，选择“通讯录 > 个呼”，从列表中选择联系人进入详情界面，然后选择“远程监听”。若配置了一键呼叫/消息实现远程监听，也可按【一键呼叫/消息】快捷键发起。
对讲机信道中出现其他通话声或杂音时，应如何处理？
可更改为新的频点，或调整静噪级别。若因未设置信令导致同频干扰，需对组内所有对讲机进行信令设置，且必须同时更改组内所有对讲机的信令设置。
What does the 'Priority interrupt' function allow you to do?
It allows you to interrupt the ongoing call, call hang, and remote monitor on the current channel to release it. Then you can initiate a new call or a new data service on that channel.
How does the Handover feature maintain communication quality?
It allows the radio to automatically register with the BS with stronger signal when the received signal strength fluctuates due to position change.
How can you temporarily remove a channel from the scan list if you do not want to hear activities on it?
Press the preprogrammed Nuisance delete key.
What is the definition of a roam list?
The roam list is a list of digital repeater channels where the radio roams.
Which accessories are compatible with the PTT & MIC Cable (ACN-02)?
The Receive-Only Swivel Earset (EH-02) and the Receive-Only Earbud (ES-01) are used with the PTT & MIC Cable (ACN-02).
KMC界面中显示“TETRA”或“DMR”代表什么含义？
这表示当前设置的终端类型。例如界面显示“TETRA”，则当前可创建TETRA终端的密钥文件包。该功能用于切换终端类型以生成对应的密钥文件包。
DMR 的全称及其中文含义是什么？
DMR 的全称是 Digital Mobile Radio，中文含义为数字移动对讲机。
SCK、TEI 和 TETRA 的中文名称分别是什么？
SCK 是静态密钥，TEI 是终端设备号，TETRA 是陆地集群无线电。
专网常用个呼联系人和组呼联系人显示在哪里？
专网常用个呼联系人和组呼联系人显示于对讲机应用的通讯录中。
专网拨号中，除个呼和组呼外的其它呼叫类型如何确定？
专网拨号中，其它呼叫类型根据输入的号码进行匹配。
在TFTSB TMO模式下，会话页面搜索可以检索组管理中的哪些内容？
收藏夹和收藏夹内的联系人、文件夹和文件夹内的联系人、扫描列表和扫描列表内的联系人。
在TFTSB TMO模式下，组管理页面的搜索功能覆盖哪些范围？
搜索范围包括收藏夹和收藏夹内的联系人、文件夹和文件夹内的联系人、扫描列表和扫描列表内的联系人。
ENS集群模式中，组管理页面支持搜索哪些对象？
支持搜索收藏夹和收藏夹内的联系人、组群和组群内的联系人。
VoLTE在掉线率和频谱利用率方面表现如何？
VoLTE的掉线率接近于零，频谱利用率达到GSM的4倍以上。
射频与基带如何获取时钟？其它时钟又是如何获取的？
射频与基带共用52MHz时钟，其它时钟采用分频或倍频方式获取。
主 PTT 键（A7 PTT）通过什么方式检测实现？
主 PTT 键由单独中断 GPIO_1 检测实现。
副 PTT 键（CAT PTT）的管脚和检测实现方式是什么？
副 PTT 键的管脚为 P12，由单独中断 CAM_RST 检测实现。
射频接收到的语音信号经 A7 处理后，分别通过哪些输出端口发送给内部喇叭、外部喇叭和蓝牙模块？
发送给内部喇叭通过 RIGHT_LOP 和 RIGHT_LOM 输出；发送给外部喇叭通过 LEFT_LOP 和 LEFT_LOM 输出；发送给蓝牙模块通过 MONO_LOP 和 MONO_LOM 输出。
发射信号在经过多级放大和阻抗匹配后，最终依次经过哪些组件？
最后发射信号经过收发通路切换开关进入低通滤波器。
射频发射链路中，信号经过低通滤波器处理后通过什么部件发射出去？
信号经过收发切换开关和低通滤波器过滤抑制谐波及杂散信号后，最后通过天线发射出去。
DSP产生的数据如何通过两点调制实现平衡，其调制频率响应指标是多少？
DSP产生的压缩语音数据和4FSK比特转换到符号后，一路输出到DAC生成4电平调制符号（+1、-1、+3和-3）对VCO进行高口调制，另一路输出到PLL IC进行直接调制。当这两路信号的相位与幅度达到一定比例时，两点调制达到平衡，调制频率（100Hz～7kHz）响应达到±0.4dB平坦度。
在 EC200U CAT1 模块中，Z9200 分频器的作用是什么，它将信号分路至哪两个天线部分？
Z9200 分频器用于区分低频段（LB）和中高频段（MHB），并将信号分路至上（LB）和下（MHB）天线。
EC200U CAT1 模块的低频段上天线如何连接，并与什么天线共输出？
低频段上天线由同轴线连接至外置 SMA 座，与窄带天线共天线输出。
EC200U CAT1 模块的中高频段天线位于何处？
中高频段天线位于前壳下方天线支架。
输入-80dBm射频信号时，C6015处的正常输出信号幅度应满足什么条件？
输入-80dBm的射频信号，在C6015进行输出信号幅度测试，正常情况下，输出信号幅度大于-70dBm。
发射部分的调测项包括哪些内容？
发射部分的调测项包括参考频率、发射功率和调制平衡。
进入发射功率调测界面后，系统默认调整哪些信道的功率值？
系统默认开始调整第一个信道的所有功率值。
如何调整 HP8921 和 Tuner 设置以使 AClevel 达到额定值？
设置 HP8921 输出“-47dBm/Frequency（当前信道频率值）”的带调制的射频信号。设置 Tuner 界面上的“宽窄带”及“SPK 增益”，使 HP8921 上显示 AClevel 为额定 1.4～1.5V。
哪些 TETRA 窄带终端同时被 Smart MDM 和 Smart MDM Lite 支持？
同时被 Smart MDM 和 Smart MDM Lite 支持的 TETRA 窄带终端有：PT350、PT310、PT590、MT680、PT890Ex。
该设备的工作电压和射频功率输出分别是多少？
工作电压为7.2V，射频功率输出为1W/3W。
哪些文件属于窄带 TETRA 终端插件？
G1_Tetra_IDS_V3.09.11.009.plug 和 PT3x_IDS_V4.2.01.004.plug
How should the ISSI Flag and GSSI Flag be configured to encrypt private and group numbers respectively?
To encrypt a private number, set the ISSI Flag to 1; otherwise, set it to 0. To encrypt a group number, set the GSSI Flag to 1; otherwise, set it to 0.
What are the steps to add a Conventional AIE key in a DMR system?
Enter the key name, set Type as DMR, set Key Type as AIE, set Model, click OK, click New, and then configure the key length and value.
In DMO mode, what do the status indicators reveal about the availability and connection state of gateways and repeaters?
In DMO, indicators distinguish between devices that are available and connected versus those that are available but unconnected. This applies to both gateways and repeaters.
What is the process for the BT Location feature to report location information?
After detecting the beacon information broadcast by the BT beacon, the radio sends the location information to the BT location data center through the public network.
What happens when a party's transmitting duration reaches the preset limit with the channel reservation feature turned on?
The radio of that party automatically enters the channel reservation status, allowing the other party to press the PTT key to speak. This process repeats until the cycle times expire.
How can you configure gateway information for PSTN or PABX in TMO?
Tap PSTN gateway or PABX gateway, and then set the gateway information. If configured with multiple gateway addresses, you can select the call gateway and the message gateway.
How does Energy Saving Mode affect data reception from the BS and what determines the receiving interval?

In Energy Saving Mode, the radio receives data from the BS periodically instead of continuously. The receiving interval is subject to the energy saving level, where a higher level indicates a longer interval.
身份证识别、嫌疑人鉴别和执法录像等工作依赖什么能力？
数据传输能力。
当终端分别工作在集群模式和XPT模式时，尝试开始抓取Trace会有什么提示或行为？
若终端工作在集群模式，弹出提示框“模式不支持，是否切换工作模式开始？ ”，点击“确认”则切换至常规模式，点击“取消”则停留在Trace界面。若终端工作在XPT模式，弹出提示框“请切换至常规模式”。
What are the maximum numbers of DMR and TETRA narrowband radios that can be connected to one IDS?
For narrowband radios, the maximum capacity per IDS is 6 DMR radios or 24 TETRA radios.
为确保PDC680符合职业或受控环境中的辐射限制要求，发送时间有何限制？
发送时间不得超过额定因数的 50%（最高 50%的时间发射）。
PDC680对讲机在哪些状态下不会产生射频能量辐射？
接收（收听）和待机时均不会产生射频能量辐射，仅在发射（讲话）时产生。
在集群模式下，主叫方显示红色快闪指示灯意味着什么？
在集群模式下，红色快闪表示正在建立呼叫（主叫方显示）。
集群系统中开启从属组功能后，主组成员在什么情况下会被强行拉入主组呼叫？
当主组建立呼叫时，在可抢占范围内，正在参与个呼、从属组组呼及其他类型呼叫（除紧急呼叫）的主组成员均会切换到主组呼叫中。
集群模式下对讲机如何实现网络自动切换？
集群模式下，对讲机开启 RoIP 网络并成功登记后，超出网络覆盖范围时，根据宽窄网络信号自动切换网络。
在常规模式下，如何设置某个信道的发射功率？
点击“对讲机联系人”或“对讲机”，点击“区域”，选择某个数字信道或模拟信道并点击，然后设置发射功率。
在常规模式数字信道下，如何进行对讲机检查操作？
点击“对讲机联系人”或“对讲机”，点击“通讯录”，选择“常用”或“个呼”列表中的个呼联系人，进入联系人详情界面，选择发起补充业务。
E2EE、FOACSU 和 OACSU 分别代表什么中文含义？
E2EE 代表端到端加密；FOACSU 代表手动摘机呼叫；OACSU 代表自动摘机呼叫。
对讲机在集群模式下主叫方显示红色快闪代表什么状态？
代表正在建立呼叫。
Where can declarations of essential or potentially essential IPRs notified to ETSI be found?

Declarations of essential or potentially essential IPRs notified to ETSI can be found in ETSI SR 000 314: "Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs); Essential, or potentially Essential, IPRs notified to ETSI in respect of ETSI standards", which is available from the ETSI Secretariat. Latest updates are available on the ETSI IPR online database.
Has ETSI carried out any investigation regarding the essentiality of IPRs, including IPR searches?
No, pursuant to the ETSI Directives including the ETSI IPR Policy, no investigation regarding the essentiality of IPRs, including IPR searches, has been carried out by ETSI.
For whose benefit are the 3GPP, LTE, and 5G logos registered as trademarks of ETSI?
They are registered for the benefit of ETSI Members and of the 3GPP Organizational Partners.
Which ETSI Technical Committee produced this Technical Report?
It was produced by ETSI Technical Committee TETRA and Critical Communications Evolution (TCCE).
What is the specific subject covered in part 7 of the multi-part deliverable on Terrestrial Trunked Radio (TETRA)?
Part 7 covers TETRA High-Speed Data (HSD) and TETRA Enhanced Data Service (TEDS).
What specific evaluation regarding TETRA 2 terminals is included in the document that is not covered in the standard?
The document evaluates the effect of using TETRA 2 terminals in high velocity environments such as trainborne, which is not included in the standard.
What does 'acknowledged data transfer' refer to?
It is a service provided by the layer below which gives an acknowledgement back over the air interface from the lower layer peer entity.
What is adjacent-channel interference?
Adjacent-channel interference is interference caused by coupling from a signal in an adjacent channel.
What are the characteristics and requirements of an advanced link?

An advanced link is a bidirectional connection-oriented path between an MS and a BS using acknowledged service, or a unidirectional connection-oriented path between a BS and one or several MSs using unacknowledged service. It provides windowing, segmentation, extended error protection, and choice among several throughputs, and requires a set-up phase.
How is the air-interface defined in trunked and direct modes?
The air-interface is the wireless interface between a base station and a mobile station in trunked mode, or between two mobile stations in direct mode.
What distinguishes announced cell reselection?
In announced cell reselection, the MS MLE informs the SwMI in both the old cell (leaving cell) and the new cell (arriving cell) that a cell change is performed.
What components make up the burst header?
The burst header consists of a burst identifier carrying a SICH channel for all burst types, plus an AACH channel for the NDB.
What is co-channel interference?
Co-channel interference is interference between two different communication channels re-using the same frequency.
Which channels comprise the common control channels transmitted by the infrastructure?
The common control channels comprise the π/4-DQPSK Main Control CHannel (MCCH) or QAM Main Control CHannel (MCCH-Q), and common Secondary Control Channels (common SCCH).
How does a conforming channel differ from a concentric channel?

A concentric channel has essentially the same azimuthal radiation pattern as the main carrier and is radiated from the same site. A conforming channel meets these criteria but also has essentially the same range and coverage area as the main carrier. A conforming channel is a special case of a concentric channel.
What is the relationship between delay spread and channel frequency selectivity?
The larger the delay spread, the more pronounced the channel frequency selectivity.
How is doppler spread defined in terms of carrier frequency and MS speed?
Doppler spread is the maximum doppler shift undergone by the received carrier, calculated as the product of carrier frequency by the ratio of MS speed to light propagation speed.
What is the effect of increased doppler spread on channel time selectivity?
The larger the doppler spread, the more pronounced the channel time selectivity.
What is the maximum supported separation between an eccentric channel’s transmitter site and the main carrier’s transmitter site according to TETRA standard ETSI EN 300 392-2?
Up to a maximum separation of 4 km.
What characterizes frequency-selective fading?
Frequency-selective fading is distortion on channel frequency response due to multipath propagation, giving rise to variable attenuation (selectivity) and phase rotation with frequency.
Can multiple users share the same Individual TetRA Subscriber Identity (ITSl)?
No, an ITSl cannot be shared by multiple users.
Which procedures perform initial cell selection?
Initial cell selection is performed by procedures located in the MLE and in the MAC.
What does link adaptation involve on D8PSK and QAM channels?
Link adaptation involves adaptively changing the modulation level on a D8PSK channel, or the modulation level and/or coding rate on a QAM channel.
What is a MAC block?
A MAC block is the unit of information transferred between the upper MAC and lower MAC for a particular logical channel.
Where is the Main Control Channel (MCCH) located in a conventional access cell?
The MCCH is located on timeslot 1 of the main carrier.
What are the three types of monitoring defined in the text?

The three types of monitoring are neighbour cell monitoring (monitoring of the main carrier on adjacent cells), irregular channel monitoring (monitoring of irregular carriers on the serving cell or on adjacent cells), and main carrier monitoring (monitoring of the main carrier on the serving cell).
What characteristics define a non-conforming concentric channel?

A non-conforming concentric channel has essentially the same azimuthal radiation pattern as the main carrier and is radiated from the same site as the main carrier, but it has a different range and coverage area from the main carrier.
What defines normal mode operation regarding MCCH or MCCH-Q presence?
Normal mode is a mode of operation in which the MCCH is present in timeslot 1 of all frames 1 to 18, or in which the MCCH-Q is present in at least timeslot 1 of all frames 1 to 18.
How is a physical channel defined in this context?
A physical channel is defined as a timeslot plus its associated uplink and downlink frequency allocation.
What characterizes quasi-transmission trunking regarding channel allocation and de-allocation?

In quasi-transmission trunking, a traffic channel is allocated for each call transaction while the pressel is activated. Additionally, channel de-allocation is delayed for a short period at the end of the transaction after the pressel release.
What are the inputs required for the ranking procedure?
The inputs to the ranking procedure are outputs from the monitoring and/or scanning process and network parameters received in the MLE broadcast.
What is the purpose of the scrambling process?
Scrambling is the process of randomizing the bit sequence to avoid eavesdropping and to distinguish base stations from each other.
What is a segment in the context of TL-SDU?
A segment is a numbered piece of a TL-SDU that normally fits into one MAC layer PDU.
How does a semi-super-sectored channel differ from the main carrier in terms of azimuthal extent?

A semi-super-sectored channel has an azimuthal extent that exceeds the azimuthal extent of the main carrier in one azimuthal direction and is less than the azimuthal extent of the main carrier in the other azimuthal direction. It is radiated from the same site as the main carrier.
What causes time-selective fading?
Time-selective fading is caused by the variation of channel attenuation in time due to MS motion.
Which layer provides the TM-SDU?
The TM-SDU is the SDU from the layer above the MAC, which is the LLC.
How does transmission trunking allocate traffic channels?
In transmission trunking, the traffic channel is individually allocated for each call transaction in a circuit mode call, specifically for each activation of the presssel.
What distinguishes unannounced cell reselection from undeclared cell reselection regarding notification?
In unannounced cell reselection, the MS MLE does not inform the old cell but informs the new cell. In undeclared cell reselection, the MS MLE does not inform either the old cell or the new cell.
What does the acronym AACH stand for?
Access Assignment Channel
What does BSCH-Q represent?
Broadcast Synchronization Channel, QAM
What is the definition of the term BUX?
Bad Urban scenario in conjunction with an MS speed of $x$ km/h
What does the acronym ETSI stand for?
European Telecommunications Standards Institute
What does HTx represent in the context of terrain scenarios and MS speed?
Hilly Terrain scenario in conjunction with an MS speed of x km/h
What is the net rate of the TCH/7,2 traffic channel?
The net rate is 7,2 kbit/s.
Which modulation scheme is used for the TCH-P8/10,8 traffic channel and what is its net rate?
It uses π/8-D8PSK modulation with a net rate of 10,8 kbit/s.
How is the TUx scenario defined in terms of MS speed?
TUx refers to the Typical Urban scenario in conjunction with an MS speed of x km/h.
What functions does MEX perform in the TETRA protocol stack?
MEX performs routing and filtering, and may manage the relative precedence of packet data in cases where packet data flow is constrained by air-interface bandwidth limitations.
How does the Mobile Link Entity (MLE) manage mobile connections and protocol discrimination?

The Mobile Link Entity (MLE) manages the mobile connection, such as selecting a new serving cell when the present serving cell fails, and performs protocol discrimination by routing to the higher layer entities.
What collective term is used for MM, CMCE, and SNDCP in the TETRA protocol?
MM, CMCE, and SNDCP are collectively called sub-network access functions (SNAFs).
How is the interaction between layers and sublayers described in the TETRA protocol?
The interaction between the layers and sublayers is described in terms of Service Access Points (SAPs), and service primitives and their parameters.
How does U-plane traffic enter the MAC layer?

U-plane traffic, which includes voice and circuit mode data, along with end-to-end user signalling, enters the MAC directly from the U-plane application through a dedicated Service Access Point (SAP).
What enhancements were incorporated into the TETRA standard since the publication of ETSI EN 300 392-2 V3.2.1?

The enhancements include Direct Access (DA), more efficient acknowledgements for the extended advanced link, support of frequency range down to 138 MHz for π/4-DQPSK modulation, and new channel types such as super-sectored channels and eccentric channels.
What is Conventional Access in the context of TETRA standards?
Conventional Access is a method of operation where access to HSD channels is allowed only via a TETRA 1 (π/4-DQPSK) control channel, as specified in ETSI EN 300 392-2 V3.2.1.
What new channel bandwidths were introduced to the standard alongside the existing 25 kHz bandwidth for HSD channels?
Three new channel bandwidths were introduced: 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz.
How does a TETRA 1 mobile station interact with an enhanced base station that supports both TETRA 1 and HSD?
A TETRA 1 mobile station communicates via the enhanced base station and common infrastructure using all TETRA 1 network services and facilities, while ignoring any HSD related signalling.
What is the registration process for an HSD enabled mobile station before it can request capacity on an HSD channel?
The mobile station first registers in the traditional way via the TETRA 1 main control channel to inform the infrastructure of its HSD capabilities.
Which modulation schemes are introduced for the HSD air interface to boost system data throughput, and how do they relate to the TETRA 1 standard?

The HSD air interface introduces four spectral-efficient multilevel modulation schemes: π/8-D8PSK, 4-QAM, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM. These schemes add to the π/4-DQPSK modulation scheme used in the TETRA 1 standard.
What are the sub-carrier spacing and the corresponding number of sub-carriers for each channel bandwidth in Multi-Carrier filterbank-based signalling?
The sub-carriers are spaced at 2.7 kHz. The number of sub-carriers used corresponds to the channel bandwidths as follows: 8 sub-carriers for 25 kHz, 16 for 50 kHz, 32 for 100 kHz, and 48 for 150 kHz.
What channel encoding schemes and rates are adopted for payload and header blocks in the HSD air interface?

For payload channel encoding, a turbo-coding scheme is adopted with rates 1/2, 2/3, and rate 1 (unencoded case). For short header blocks, a separate block channel encoding using Reed Muller is adopted to enable reliable slot decoding and network operations.
How do link adaptation techniques improve system performance in the HSD air interface?

Link adaptation techniques improve system performance, such as overall message throughput, by adaptively choosing the modulation level, the coding rate, and possibly the RF channel bandwidth according to varying channel propagation conditions.
How can sectored antennas extend the HSD channel range without requiring additional base station sites?

Sectored antennas, such as directional panel antennas, allow a set of sectored, high RF bandwidth channels to cover the full area of a TETRA 1 main control channel from a single base station site, thereby extending the HSD channel range to match that of a TETRA 1 control channel.
What is the function of a fully super-sectored channel introduced in V3.7.1 of ETSI EN 300 392-2?

A fully super-sectored channel can serve as an umbrella channel with a circular coverage area, allowing mobile stations from multiple co-sited sectored cells (which have non-circular service areas) to use it.
What are the three classes of data defined for HSD channel higher layer protocols and their respective characteristics?

The three classes are: 1) Real-time class: for applications that cannot tolerate delivery delay; 2) Telemetry class: for applications with intermittent data which can tolerate moderate delivery delay and packet loss; 3) Background class: for applications that are intolerant of packet loss.
What is the purpose of the "scheduled access" mechanism introduced in the enhanced TETRA protocols?

Scheduled access facilitates the transmission of real-time data and telemetry applications by providing capacity to an application at regular time intervals, eliminating the need for random access requests each time.
How does the "data priority" mechanism function in the context of packet data transmission?
The data priority mechanism enables the Mobile Station (MS) to indicate a priority for obtaining reserved slots from the Base Station (BS) for packet data transmission.
Which applications are classified under the background class for transmission over TETRA HSD channels?

Examples of the background class include general file transfer; transfer of photographs and maps; reliable delivery of dispatch messages with attached maps, plans, photographs and documents; secure delivery of patient and client records; and database enquiries such as police national computer.
Why is TETRA HSD considered advantageous over commercial 3G networks for public safety and emergency relief users?

TETRA 2 standard is designed to the same level of security as TETRA 1 standard, which provides an advantage for TETRA HSD services compared to those in commercial 3G networks for public safety and emergency relief users.
How does the TETRA high-speed data HSD air interface relate to the TETRA 1 air interface?
The TETRA high-speed data HSD air interface follows closely the TETRA 1 air interface for backwards compatibility purposes.
What is the difference between full FDD and half FDD operation for Mobile Stations (MSs) in TETRA systems?

In full Frequency Division Duplex (FDD), uplink and downlink frequencies are operational at the same time. In half FDD, uplink and downlink are operational alternately, depending on the capability of the MS.
How is a physical channel formed in the TETRA high-speed air interface TDMA structure?
A physical channel is formed by a pair of timeslots associated with a pair of FDD RF frequencies. This physical channel conveys traffic and signalling messages as logical channels.
What are the radio characteristics of the main carrier for Conventional Access in a TETRA system enhanced with high speed capability?

For Conventional Access, the main carrier has the following characteristics: modulation is $\pi/4$-DQPSK, gross transmission rate is $36 \mathrm{kbit} / \mathrm{s}$, duplex spacing varies according to frequency allocation, and RF carrier spacing is $25 \mathrm{kHz}$.
What modulation types are introduced by the TETRA HSD air interface in addition to π/4-DQPSK?
The TETRA HSD air interface introduces π/8-D8PSK, 4-QAM, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM.
Which bandwidth channels have been introduced for QAM to boost data throughput besides the existing 25 kHz channel?
The new higher bandwidth channels introduced for QAM are 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz.
For Direct Access, what is the main carrier modulation and what are its possible bandwidths?
For Direct Access, the main carrier uses QAM modulation, and its bandwidth can be 25 kHz, 50 kHz, 100 kHz, or 150 kHz.
How does the symbol structure within a timeslot differ between phase modulation and QAM?

For phase modulation, a timeslot corresponds to 255 symbol durations, each lasting $500 / 9 \mu \mathrm{s}$ (approximately $55.56 \mu \mathrm{s}$). For QAM, a timeslot is divided into 34 modulation symbol durations, each lasting $5 / 12 \mathrm{~ms}$ (approximately $416.7 \mu \mathrm{s}$).
What is the timing delay between the start of downlink and uplink structures at the BS, and what is its purpose?

The start of the hyperframe, multiframe, and TDMA frame received at the BS is delayed by a fixed period of 2 timeslots from the start of the corresponding downlink structures. This delay enables the MS to respond to downlink signalling within the associated uplink frame.
Why is the downlink transmission capacity slightly greater than the uplink capacity in the TETRA slot structure?
The downlink capacity is greater due to the need to ramp up the MS transmitter power and linearize the MS power amplifier.
How much additional gross capacity does the π/4-DQPSK downlink slot have compared to the uplink, and what is this extra capacity used for?
The π/4-DQPSK downlink slot has approximately 30 bits more gross capacity, which is used to transmit "low layer" MAC information.
What are the designations of the field containing extra downlink capacity at the physical and MAC levels, and is it visible above the MAC level?
At the physical level, the field is designated the "broadcast block," and at the MAC level, it is designated the Access Assignment CHannel (AACH). This field is not visible above the MAC level.
What information does the usage marker convey on traffic channels?
The usage marker indicates the intended destination of the downlink slot and the allowed user of the uplink slot.
How many symbol periods are in one timeslot?
One timeslot equals 255 symbol periods.
How does the information structure in QAM channel slots differ from that in phase modulation channels?

In QAM channels, full or sub-slots carry single blocks of information, whereas phase modulation channels carry two separate blocks with an insertion of training sequence blocks or broadcast blocks between them.
Why is the downlink transmission capacity slightly greater than the uplink capacity in this system?
The downlink capacity is greater because of the need to ramp up and down the MS transmitter power and to allow for guard periods.
What are the six types of symbols multiplexed in the QAM channel information field?
The six symbol types are: frequency correction symbols, synchronization symbols, secondary synchronization symbols, pilot symbols, header symbols, and data symbols.
What is the specific function of pilot symbols in the receiver?
Pilot symbols have known values and pre-arranged positions, and they are used in the receiver for channel (propagation condition) estimation.
What is the function of the AACH-Q in QAM channels?
The AACH-Q plays a similar role in QAM channels as AACH in phase modulation channels and is transmitted in the downlink only via some of the header symbols.
What information do header symbols other than those carrying AACH-Q indicate?
Other header symbols are used, on both uplink and downlink, to indicate the modulation level and the coding rate of the payload.
Which burst type is restricted to using only $\pi/4$-DQPSK modulation?
Burst type 6 uses $\pi/4$-DQPSK modulation only.
What modulation schemes are available for the five burst types other than burst type 6?
The other five burst types may use either $\pi/4$-DQPSK or $\pi/8$-D8PSK modulation.
How many modulation symbol periods constitute one time slot?
One time slot equals 255 modulation symbols periods.
What is the purpose of the Control Burst (CB) in the QAM system?
The CB is used by the MS to transmit reserved access control messages to the BS.
What are the transmission characteristics and usage of the Random Access Burst (RAB)?
The RAB is transmitted in the uplink, uses 8 sub-carriers and 4-QAM for all QAM channel bandwidths, and is used by the MS to transmit random access control messages to the BS.
How does the Linearization Uplink Burst (LB) differ from other bursts in terms of content and timing?
The LB contains no useful symbols, and its timing is determined only by the time mask. It may be used by MSs to linearize their transmitters.
What information does the Frequency Correction Burst (FCB) broadcast on a Direct Access cell?

On a Direct Access cell, the FCB is used by the BS to broadcast synchronization information and essential system information needed by an MS to synchronize with and use the facilities of a DA cell. On 50 kHz, 100 kHz, or 150 kHz channels, it may also contain other downlink signalling.
What is the duration of one time slot in terms of modulation symbol periods?
One time slot equals 34 modulation symbols periods.
How are subslots structured within a time slot regarding modulation symbol periods?
A time slot is divided into two subslots, where subslot 1 consists of 17 modulation symbols periods and subslot 2 consists of 17 modulation symbols periods.
How is the physical content of a timeslot or subslot arranged in QAM channels?

In QAM channels, the physical content of a timeslot or subslot, known as the high-speed data burst, is arranged in both the frequency and time domain according to the symbol patterns depicted in figure 6.5.
Which QAM bursts are introduced in clause 6.4.2?
The QAM bursts introduced in clause 6.4.2 are CB, RAB, LB, NUB, NDB, LDB, and FCB.
Why are pilot and synchronization symbols transmitted only in 4-QAM?
They are transmitted only in 4-QAM to allow more robust conditions for channel estimation and synchronization recovery.
What are the possible numbers of sub-carriers and their corresponding overall bandwidths?
The possible numbers of sub-carriers are 8, 16, 32, and 48, corresponding to overall bandwidths of 25 kHz, 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz respectively.
Besides synchronization recovery, what additional function do synchronization symbols serve in channel estimation?
The synchronization symbols are also used as additional pilot symbols in channel estimation.
What are the two categories of logical channels in phase modulation and what type of information does each carry?
The two categories are control channels, which carry signalling messages and packet data, and traffic channels, which carry speech or data information in circuit switched mode.
Which control channel category is the exception to the rule that all channels use π/4-DQPSK modulation, and what modulation schemes can it use?
The Signalling Channel (SCH), which is category 2, is the exception. It uses either π/4-DQPSK or π/8-D8PSK modulation.
What are the two defined categories of the Broadcast Control Channel (BCCH) and their specific functions?

The two categories are the Broadcast Network Channel (BNCH), used for downlink only to broadcast network information to MSs, and the Broadcast Synchronization Channel (BSCH), used for downlink only to broadcast information for frequency, time, and scrambling synchronization of the MSs.
How does the notation for Signalling Channels change when π/8-D8PSK modulation is used, and can you provide an example?
When π/8-D8PSK modulation is used, the SCH notation changes to SCH-P8. For example, SCH/HD changes to SCH-P8/HD.
What is the function of the Access Assignment Channel (AACH) and where is it present?
The AACH is present on all transmitted downlink slots and is used to indicate the assignment of uplink and downlink slots on each physical channel. It is internal to the MAC.
What are the two categories of Linearization Channel (LCH) and how are they used?
The two categories are the Common Linearization Channel (CLCH), which is used in the uplink and shared by all MSs, and the BS Linearization Channel (BLCH), which is used in the downlink by the BS.
What are the two categories of the BCCH-Q channel and their respective functions?

The two categories are Broadcast Network Channel (BNCH-Q), which broadcasts network information from the BS to all MSs, and Broadcast Synchronization Channel (BSCH-Q), which broadcasts information for frequency, time, and scrambling synchronization of Direct Access MSs as well as network information.
Under what conditions is the SCH-Q/B signalling channel used and decoded by MSs?

SCH-Q/B is used only in the downlink direction on 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz channels (in the FCB). It uses 4-QAM modulation and a 1/2 coding rate. Only MSs that understand the FCB value in the SICH-Q/D will decode the SCH-Q/B.
How are the SCH-Q/D, SCH-Q/U, and SCH-Q/HU signalling channels subdivided?
These signalling channels are subdivided according to modulation (4-QAM, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM), coding rates (1/2, 2/3, and 1), and channel bandwidth (25 kHz, 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz).
What information does the Slot Information Channel (SICH-Q) convey in uplink and downlink transmissions?

In both uplink (SICH-Q/U) and downlink (SICH-Q/D), SICH-Q indicates the modulation and coding used in the remainder of the slot or subslot. Additionally, the downlink SICH-Q indicates whether the burst is an FCB.
How are the Common Linearization Channel (CLCH-Q) and BS Linearization Channel (BLCH-Q) utilized?

The Common Linearization Channel (CLCH-Q) is used in the uplink and is shared by all the MSs. The BS Linearization Channel (BLCH-Q) is used in the downlink by the BS. Both are used by the BS and MS to linearize their transmitters.
Which logical channels form the headers in downlink and uplink bursts, and what modulation do they use?
Logical channels AACH-Q and SICH-Q/D form the header in downlink bursts, while SICH-Q/U forms the header in uplink bursts. These headers use 4-QAM.
What are the coding characteristics and frequency placement of the headers in QAM bursts?

The headers employ Reed Muller coding with a coding rate of 5/16. The header symbols are placed on sub-carriers occupying the central 25 kHz of QAM bursts on the frequency axis, regardless of the channel bandwidth, to increase robustness in a multi-path environment.
Which modulation scheme is used by logical channels and burst types marked with an asterisk (*) in the first table?
Logical channels and burst types marked with an asterisk (*) use π/8-D8PSK modulation.
What are the direction and burst types for the SCH/HU logical channel?
The SCH/HU logical channel operates in the Uplink direction and uses the CB burst type.
What modulation and coding specifications apply to AACH-Q, SICH-Q/D, and SICH-Q/U logical channels?
AACH-Q, SICH-Q/D, and SICH-Q/U use sub-carriers within the central 25 kHz of the frequency axis, are modulated with 4-QAM, and use 5/16 rate coding.
What is the channel bandwidth for all physical channels mentioned in the note?
All physical channels are 25 kHz channels.
Which sub-carriers does SCH-Q/B use on 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz channels?
On 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz channels, SCH-Q/B uses the outer sub-carriers of the frequency axis, which are the sub-carriers not within the central 25 kHz.
How does the content of the FCB differ between 25 kHz QAM channels and 50/100/150 kHz QAM channels?
On a 50 kHz, 100 kHz, or 150 kHz QAM channel, the FCB contains both the BSCH-Q and SCH-Q/B logical channels. On a 25 kHz QAM channel, the FCB contains only the BSCH-Q logical channel.
What are the modulation rates for π/4-DQPSK and π/8-D8PSK in the base-band part of phase modulation channels?
The modulation rate is 36 kbit/s for π/4-DQPSK and 54 kbit/s for π/8-D8PSK.
What are the three types of Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) used in the base-band part of QAM channels?
The three types of QAM used are 4-QAM, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM.
How many sub-carriers are used per 25 kHz in QAM channels, and how does this scale for 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz channels?
There are 8 sub-carriers per 25 kHz. This scales to 8, 16, 32, and 48 sub-carriers for 25 kHz, 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz channels respectively.
What constraint applies to the phase angle of pilot and synchronization sub-carrier symbols?

Pilot and synchronization sub-carrier symbols are not constrained to lie on constellation points; they can take on any phase angle as long as the magnitude of these symbols corresponds to the synchronization/pilot locus.
Which locus is selected for pilot, synchronization, and header sub-carrier symbols, and why?
A circle of unity amplitude is selected because this locus is independent of the modulation.
What modulation scheme do header sub-carrier symbols use, and where are they located in the complex plane?
Header sub-carrier symbols lie on the circle of unity amplitude and use 4-QAM in all three cases.
Which modulation types are permitted on all four channel bandwidths (25 kHz, 50 kHz, 100 kHz, and 150 kHz) in TETRA high-speed channels?
QAM modulations are permitted on all four channel bandwidths.
What is the maximum gross bit rate offered by 64-QAM 4-slot modulation across the available channel bandwidths?
The maximum gross bit rate offered by 64-QAM 4-slot modulation is 691 kbit/s, which occurs on the 150 kHz channel.
How are information bits protected in TETRA HSD logical channels before being mapped onto channel symbols?

Information bits are protected by means of one or two coding schemes followed by interleaving and scrambling. These operations are carried out at the binary level prior to mapping of bits onto channel symbols.
What is the primary purpose of coding in communication systems?
Coding is used to reduce the occurrence of errors due to noise, interference, distortion, and other channel impairments, and also to detect errors in the decoded binary stream.
How does the two-level coding scheme work for logical channels carried by burst payloads?

First, a Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) block encoder appends 16 redundant bits to the information block for error detection. Then, this is concatenated with a more powerful code: a Rate Compatible Punctured Convolutional code for phase modulation, or a Parallel Concatenated Convolutional code for QAM, which aims to reduce error occurrence at the cost of spectrum efficiency.
Which logical channels do not employ CRC coding, and what coding method do they use instead?
Logical channels using the header section of the QAM burst and the AACH for phase modulation do not employ CRC coding. They rely on single-level powerful Reed-Muller block codes.
Which encoders are used to generate type-3 bits from type-2 bits?

Type-3 bits are generated by encoding type-2 bits using either a convolutional encoder for phase modulation or a parallel concatenated convolutional encoder for QAM. This encoding level may be missing in some cases, such as QAM uncoded payload channels.
Describe the processing steps that transform type-3 bits into type-5 bits.
Type-3 bits are first reordered and interleaved to become type-4 bits (packed in a type-4 block). Then, type-4 bits are scrambled to become type-5 bits, which compose a type-5 block.
What are the five kinds of multiplexed blocks that type-5 blocks are mapped into?
A multiplexed block may be one of five different kinds: control block, broadcast block (BBK), synchronization block, block-1 block, or block-2 block.
Which clauses detail the coding techniques for channels using phase modulation and QAM respectively?
Coding techniques are detailed in clauses 6.8.4 and 6.8.5 for channels using phase modulation and QAM, respectively.
In which clause is scrambling discussed?
Scrambling is discussed in clause 6.8.8.
What are the specific RCPC code rates used for TCH/4,8 and TCH/2,4 logical channels in Stage 2?
The RCPC code rate is 292/432 for TCH/4,8 and 148/432 for TCH/2,4.
What are the K and K' values for the BSCH logical channel in π/4-DQPSK?
For the BSCH logical channel in π/4-DQPSK, the K value is 60 and the K' value is 120.
How are header section channels like SICH-Q/U and AACH-Q protected in QAM channels?
Header section channels such as SICH-Q/U, SCH-Q/D, and AACH-Q are protected by means of a block Reed-Muller (RM) code followed by interleaving and scrambling.
Which logical channel is borne by the header sections of the NUB and CB?
The SICH-Q/U logical channel is borne by the header sections of the NUB and CB.
After the RM block code, what are the subsequent processing steps for the SICH-Q/U sequence?
The sequence is fed to the interleaver, which modifies the order of bits without changing the sequence length, and finally to the scrambling unit.
How is the final 64-bit sequence for SICH-Q/D constructed before interleaving and scrambling?
The 16-bit coded sequence from SICH-Q/D is merged with the 48-bit sequence representing the AACH-Q channel.
How is the 15-bit input sequence of the AACH-Q channel processed?
The 15-bit input sequence is subdivided into three consecutive 5-bit sub-sequences. Each sub-sequence is fed to a (16,5) RM block code to generate a 16-bit coded sub-sequence.
Which input bits generate the coded sub-sequence [b_o(33), ..., b_o(48)] in the AACH-Q channel?
The input sub-sequence [b_i(11), b_i(12), ..., b_i(15)] generates the coded sub-sequence [b_o(33), b_o(34), ..., b_o(48)].
What is the bit length of the final encoded sequence formed by appending a 48-bit sequence to the SICH-Q/D logical channel representation, and what processing blocks does it enter next?
The final encoded sequence is 64 bits long. It is subsequently fed to the interleaving and scrambling blocks.
How is the input sequence processed for the SCH-Q/HU logical channel before encoding or interleaving?
The input sequence of K-16 information bits is passed through a CRC encoder, which appends 16 CRC bits to yield a sequence of K bits.
What additional bits are appended to the K input bits when using a PCCC turbo encoder for the SCH-Q/HU channel?
Three termination bits are appended to the sequence of K input bits.
What determines the length K' of the PCCC encoded sequence for the SCH-Q/HU channel?
K' depends on the coding rate and the payload capacity, specifically the number of subcarriers and the modulation level.
How does the encoding procedure for the SCH-Q/U logical channel compare to that of the SCH-Q/HU logical channel?
The encoding procedure for the SCH-Q/U logical channel is identical to that outlined for the SCH-Q/HU logical channel, except for the values of K and K'.
Which payload carries the SCH-Q/U logical channel?
The SCH-Q/U logical channel is carried by the NUB payload.
Which payload carries the logical channels SCH-Q/D and BNCH-Q?
The NDB payload carries the logical channels SCH-Q/D and BNCH-Q.
What is the total length of the bit sequence after CRC encoding for the SCH-Q/RA logical channel?
The total length is 81 bits, resulting from 65 information bits plus 16 appended CRC bits.
What is the output size of the PCCC turbo encoder for the SCH-Q/RA channel before interleaving and scrambling?
The PCCC encoder produces an encoded sequence of 168 bits.
Which part of the FCB payload carries the logical channel BSCH-Q?
The logical channel BSCH-Q is carried by the data set A part of the FCB payload, specifically by the part carried by the sub-carriers within the central 25 kHz of the frequency axis.
What is the bit sequence length after CRC encoding for the BSCH-Q logical channel?
The input sequence of 117 information bits is passed through a CRC encoder which appends 16 CRC bits, yielding a sequence of 133 bits.
How many bits does the PCCC encoder produce for the BSCH-Q logical channel?
The PCCC encoder produces an encoded sequence of 272 bits.
Which sub-carriers carry the logical channel SCH-Q/B?

The logical channel SCH-Q/B is carried by the data set B part of the FCB payload, which corresponds to the outer sub-carriers of the frequency axis (i.e., sub-carriers not within the central 25 kHz of the frequency axis).
How does the coding process for the downlink broadcast block differ from the standard payload data encoding?

The downlink broadcast block is encoded by a Reed-Muller block code prior to symbol mapping, whereas standard payload data uses RCPC coding after CRC encoding. Additionally, no CRC protection or interleaving is employed for the downlink broadcast block.
What are the three types of codes used on QAM channels as described in the text?

The three types are: 1) CRC encoder for burst payload data bits to provide error detection capability; 2) Parallel Concatenated Convolutional Code (PCCC) for payload data bits equipped with CRC bits to provide robustness against channel impairments, or leaving them uncoded in some cases; 3) Reed-Muller block code for the header section of the burst prior to interleaving, with no CRC protection.
What factors determine the sizes of the input and output data blocks for QAM channel encoding?
The sizes depend on the logical channel they are associated with, the modulation format, and the PCCC coding rate employed.
How many tail bits are appended to each block before encoding by the RSC encoders, and what is their purpose?
Three tail bits are appended to each of the two blocks (original and interleaved) to force the final state of the respective RSCs to zero.
Describe the processing order for the two constituent encoders in the PCCC scheme.
One constituent encoder processes the bits in their natural order of presentation, while the other processes an interleaved version of the same block produced by the inner interleaver.
What is the primary benefit of the quadratic-congruence interleaving technique regarding memory usage?
The interleaved bit positions are calculated in real time as the interleaving procedure goes on, with no need to pre-store them in memory, which permits to save on memory size.
How is the sequence of indices $c_{m}$ calculated in the first step of the quadratic-congruence block interleaver algorithm?
The sequence is calculated where $S$ is the smallest power of 2 larger or equal than $K$, with $c_{0}=0$ and $c_{m}=[c_{m-1}+m] \bmod S$ for $m=1,2, \cdots, S-1$.
How do the interleaving methods for high-speed π/8-D8PSK logical channels compare to those used in original TETRA π/4-DQPSK logical channels?
The interleaving methods used for high-speed π/8-D8PSK logical channels are unchanged from those used in the original TETRA π/4-DQPSK logical channels.
What are the possible values for N when interleaving over N blocks for a sequence of M type-3 blocks?
N has values 1, 4, or 8.
What is the primary advantage of using a linear-congruence approach for bit interleaving in QAM channels?

The primary advantage is that it permits on-the-fly operation, meaning interleaved bit positions are calculated in real time as the procedure proceeds. This eliminates the need to pre-store positions in memory, which is useful for saving memory size.
Which encoders can produce the block of bits that serves as input to the QAM channel interleaver?
The interleaver operates on a block of bits emerging from a CRC, PCCC, or Reed-Muller encoder.
What are the values of K and a for the SICH-Q/U logical channel when mapping on burst headers using 4/16/64-QAM?
For the SICH-Q/U logical channel mapping on burst headers with 4/16/64-QAM, the values are K=16 and a=5.
How are the block-encoded bits for logical channels SICH-Q/D and AACH-Q processed according to the last row of table 6.15?
The block-encoded bits relevant to logical channels SICH-Q/D and AACH-Q are merged together and then interleaved.
What are the K and a values for the SCH-Q/HU logical channel on burst payloads with 50 kHz bandwidth and 64-QAM modulation?
For SCH-Q/HU with 50 kHz bandwidth and 64-QAM, K=960 and a=31.
What is the primary purpose of applying a scrambling code at the Base Station (BS)?
The primary purpose is to distinguish that BS from other BSs.
How does a Mobile Station (MS) use the scrambling code received via BSCH or BSCH-Q?

The MS uses the scrambling code to descramble the contents of all other logical channels transmitted by that BS. Using the correct scrambling code prevents the decoding of signalling information from adjacent cells, other than the BSCH or BSCH-Q.
What components make up the scrambling code contained in BSCH and BSCH-Q?
The scrambling code comprises the "colour code" plus MNI (Mobile Network Identity).
What are the frequency accuracy requirements for the BS single frequency source used for RF frequency generation and clocking the timebase?
The frequency accuracy must be better than ±0.2 ppm. For frequencies above 520 MHz, the requirement is stricter at ±0.1 ppm.
Why must a single source be used for all channels of the BS?
A single source is used to ensure that different channels transmitted by the BS are frequency synchronized.
What is the maximum allowed timing difference between the start of timeslots transmitted on different channels for time synchronization purposes?
The timing difference is required to be less than 125/9 μs. This requirement includes carriers that are carrying eccentric channels.
To which channels is the normal extended colour code applied, even when they are sent in the same burst as BSCH or BSCH-Q?
The normal extended colour code is applied to SCH/HD or BNCH, AACH, SCH-Q/B, AACH-Q, and SICH-Q/D, even when these are sent in the same burst as BSCH or BSCH-Q.
What is the maximum allowed timing difference between the timebase references of any BS pair when different BSs timeshare the same channel in a TETRA network?
The timing difference is required to be less than 250/9 μs.
Within what frequency accuracy range must an MS operate relative to the signals received from the BS?
The frequency accuracy is required to be within ±100 Hz of the signals received from the BS.
How should an MS adjust its internal timebase if the timing difference with the received BS signals exceeds 125/9 μs?
The MS should adjust its timebase in steps of not greater than 125/9 μs at intervals of not less than 1 s and not greater than 3 s until the timing difference falls below 125/9 μs.
Under what signal level and interference conditions are the MS frequency and timing accuracies required to be met?
They are required to be met at 3 dB below the reference sensitivity level and 3 dB less carrier to interference ratio than the reference interference ratio.
What is the maximum timing difference an MS may perceive when moving from an eccentric channel to a new channel, excluding further propagation delay effects?
The timing difference may be up to ±250/9 μs.
What causes the timing difference of up to ±250/9 μs when an MS moves from an eccentric channel?
It is caused by BS timing imperfections and geographical delay.
How do Conventional Access (CA) MSs obtain initial synchronization at power-up?
They obtain initial synchronization via the π/4-DQPSK synchronization burst on the BSCH logical channel.
What is the purpose of the BSCH transmitted in the downlink direction?
The BSCH enables the MS to synchronize itself to the BS and, if necessary, correct its frequency standard to align with that of the BS.
How do π/8-D8PSK modulated HSD channels maintain synchronization?
They maintain synchronization in the same way as π/4-DQPSK modulated channels using frame 18.
What are the prerequisites for correct demodulation and decoding in QAM PDCH receivers?
Accurate carrier and symbol synchronization are required, meaning the symbol timing offset τ and the carrier frequency offset ν of the incoming waveform must be properly estimated.
How are coarse estimates of symbol timing offset and carrier frequency offset obtained for CA in QAM channels?

A first coarse estimate is carried out using a π/4-DQPSK modulated synchronization burst (BSCH logical channel), which restricts uncertainty intervals to less than a symbol for τ and less than around ±100 Hz for ν.
What method is used to refine coarse synchronization estimates in QAM channels for CA?
The coarse estimates are refined by resorting to a timing recovery algorithm followed by a frequency offset estimator.
What approach is used for channel estimation?
Channel estimation is based on the Bayesian-in-time linear-interpolation-in-frequency approach outlined in clause B.2.
What is the primary function of synchronization and pilot symbols in the TETRA HSD burst format?
Their function is to facilitate symbol/frequency synchronization and channel estimation.
How are synchronization symbols distributed across subcarriers in the first signalling interval for all burst types?
Synchronization symbols are transmitted on all subcarriers in the first signalling interval for all types of bursts.
What is the difference in synchronization symbol occupancy in the second signalling interval between NUB/CB/RAB bursts and NDB/FCB bursts?
In the second interval, all subcarriers are occupied by synchronization symbols for NUB, CB, and RAB bursts, whereas only half subcarriers are occupied for NDB and FCB bursts.
How is the transmitted preamble detected and what two functions does this detection jointly achieve?

The transmitted preamble, which comprises known symbols and has a predetermined shape, is detected by means of a correlator. This detection permits to jointly achieve burst identification and timing synchronization.
How does the receiver estimate the burst time of arrival using the correlator?
At the receiver site, a local replica of the initial burst segment is correlated with the incoming waveform. The instant when the correlator peaks gives an estimate of the burst time of arrival.
What is the role of the interpolation circuit driven by the burst time of arrival estimate?

The estimate of the burst time of arrival is employed to drive an interpolation circuit that produces symbol-rate samples of the entire burst (including payload, header, and pilot sections) on each subcarrier after the demultiplexer, with small synchronization errors.
Which symbols in the burst preamble are used for the delay and multiply approach to estimate carrier frequency offset?
The same synchronization symbols in the burst preamble are employed for this purpose.
How is modulation removed from the burst preamble samples in the delay and multiply approach?
Modulation is removed by multiplying the sample by the conjugate symbol.
What is the second step in the delay and multiply approach after removing modulation?
The second step is averaging the available estimates of the differential phase between consecutive samples over the subcarriers.
How do Direct Access (DA) Mobile Stations obtain initial synchronization at power-up?
At power-up, Direct Access (DA) MSs obtain initial synchronization via the QAM Frequency Correction Burst FCB on the BSCH-Q logical channel.
On which frame and carrier is the FCB regularly transmitted in the downlink direction?
The FCB is transmitted regularly in the downlink direction on frame 18 of QAM channels on the DA main carrier.
What specific symbols does the FCB contain in addition to those included in the QAM Normal Downlink Burst?

In addition to the synchronization symbols and pilot symbols included in the QAM Normal Downlink Burst (NDB), the FCB contains 60 frequency correction symbols and a set of 8 secondary synchronization symbols.
Which symbols enable the Mobile Station to obtain time synchronization?
The synchronization symbols and secondary synchronization symbols, together with the pilot symbols, enable the MS to obtain time synchronization.
How does a DA MS maintain synchronization on QAM channels after obtaining initial synchronization using the FCB?
It maintains synchronization using the synchronization symbols and pilot symbols in QAM NDBs and further FCBs, employing the same methods described for CA MSs.
Why is the TETRA HSD signal considered resilient to propagation frequency-selective fading?
It is resilient due to its MultiCarrier (MC) structure, where data transmission occurs simultaneously over a set of N equally-spaced subcarriers.
What does channel estimation and equalization reduce to in the context of TETRA HSD QAM channels prior to decoding?
It reduces to the estimation of complex-valued random attenuations throughout the burst, followed by their removal from the received samples.
What physical phenomenon causes time-variance in the channel, and what is the normalized Doppler bandwidth under specific conditions?

The relative motion between the BS and MS produces time-variance of the channel. With a carrier frequency of 800 MHz and mobile speed of 200 km/h, the Doppler bandwidth normalized to the baud rate is up to around 0.06.
How does the fading process behave within a symbol interval and across subcarriers in the frequency domain?

Over the generic subcarrier, the fading process remains nearly constant (flat) within a symbol interval. In the frequency domain, the fading process remains nearly constant (flat) across each subcarrier for a fixed signalling interval.
In the polyphase filter-bank sample equation, what do the variables N, K, alpha, c, and w represent?

N denotes the number of subcarriers, K denotes the burst length in symbols, alpha_{n, k} is the complex-valued two-dimensional fading process to be estimated, c_{n, k} is the k-th symbol on the n-th subcarrier, and w_{n, k} is AWGN.
What assumption is made regarding frequency overlap between adjacent subcarriers, and how are simulation results handled?
For simplicity, the frequency overlap between adjacent subcarriers is ignored in the considerations. However, simulation results encompass the impact of Inter-Carrier Interference (ICI).
What is the final step in using filtered estimates of the fading process?

The final step is to use the filtered estimates to evaluate the fading process at the data symbol locations throughout the burst, covering both the time (symbol interval) and frequency (subcarrier) domains.
Compare the linear interpolation method and the Bayesian-in-time linear-interpolation-in-frequency approach for channel estimation in terms of complexity and performance.

Linear interpolation in time and frequency is conceptually simple and not computationally demanding, but it has performance limits in fast fading conditions. The Bayesian-in-time linear-interpolation-in-frequency approach is more accurate but considerably more complex than the interpolation-based method.
What is the primary objective of adaptive power control in the MS?
The primary objective is to ensure that the required quality of transmission is achieved with the least possible radiated power by adjusting the RF transmit power.
How do open loop and closed loop power control mechanisms differ in terms of control source?
Open loop is the default mechanism used by the MS to control its transmit power, whereas in closed loop, MS power changes are controlled via BS signalling.
What are the three main advantages of the power control function in a TETRA network?

The advantages are: reduction of power consumption (battery saving) in the MS, reduction of interference (co-channel and adjacent channel) in the TETRA network, and reduction of interference to other nearby networks.
How is link adaptation implemented on D8PSK and QAM channels respectively?

On D8PSK channels, link adaptation is achieved by choosing a $\pi/4$-DQPSK burst or a $\pi/8$-D8PSK burst on a slot-by-slot basis. On QAM channels, it is carried out by selecting the modulation type (4-QAM, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM) and/or coding rate (1/2, 2/3, 1) on a slot-by-slot basis.
Which layers does the TETRA standard use to support Internet Protocol (IP) packet data for Mobile Stations?
The TETRA standard supports IP packet data via the Subnetwork Dependent Convergence Protocol layer (SNDCP) and the Multimedia Exchange layer (MEX).
What procedures does the Mobility Management (MM) entity perform?

The Mobility Management (MM) entity performs procedures for registration and de-registration of an MS, attachment and detachment of group identities, requesting energy saving mode or direct mode dual watch operation, and moving to direct mode and returning to trunking mode operation.
What are the two sublayers that comprise the data link layer (layer 2)?
The data link layer (layer 2) comprises the Logical Link Control (LLC) entity and the Medium Access Control (MAC) entity.
Under what condition is the basic link offered by the LLC available?
The basic link is available whenever the MS is receiving the BS.
Which MAC sublayer is responsible for channel coding, interleaving, and scrambling?
The lower MAC performs channel coding, interleaving, and scrambling.
What is the position of the Multimedia Exchange (MEX) layer relative to the MS SNDCP?
The Multimedia Exchange (MEX) layer is located above the MS SNDCP.
What is the role of SNDCP in relation to Packet Data Protocol (PDP) contexts between an MS and the SwMI?

SNDCP negotiates and maintains Packet Data Protocol (PDP) contexts between an MS and the SwMI. These contexts can be primary or secondary, with a unique primary PDP context established for each PDP address.
How does SNDCP handle data packet buffering and transfer reliability?

SNDCP buffers data packets from multiple applications and controls packet data transfer between MS and SwMI using layer 2 services. Data transfer is unacknowledged at the SNDCP level, meaning SNDCP does not perform retransmissions itself, but it allows the application to select acknowledged or unacknowledged layer 2 service.
What is the primary function of a PDP context in SNDCP?

A PDP context stores data relating to a particular packet data flow. It binds the local radio air interface address (e.g., TETRA ITS1) to the PDP address (e.g., IP address) of an application, maintains header and data compression state tables for that flow, and stores and applies QoS information specific to the packet data flow.
What is the relationship between primary and secondary PDP contexts regarding address derivation and QoS?
A secondary PDP context derives its PDP address from a primary PDP context but generally has different QoS requirements from the primary PDP context.
What is the primary function of secondary PDP contexts in relation to downlink data packets?
Secondary PDP contexts are used by the SwMI to differentiate the QoS to be given to different data packets sent on the downlink to the same PDP address.
How does the SwMI determine whether a downlink data packet should use a secondary PDP context when QoS filter information is provided by the MS?
The SwMI compares the destination port number in the downlink data packet with the QoS filter information provided by the MS.
What action does the SwMI take if the destination port number of a downlink packet does not match any secondary PDP context's QoS filter?
The SwMI sends the packet via the primary PDP context for that PDP address.
How does the SwMI handle QoS filtering if the MS does not specify a QoS filter during the activation of a secondary PDP context?

The SwMI generates and uses an automatic QoS filter, for example by recording source port numbers of uplink data packets received via each secondary PDP context and using these to filter downlink packets based on destination IP address and destination port.
What are the three packet data classes included in the QoS information negotiated during PDP context activation?
The three packet data classes are background class, telemetry class, and real-time class.
To which link type does the MS SNDCP assign a PDP context carrying real-time class data?
A PDP context carrying real-time class data should be assigned to the unacknowledged basic link.
How should the SwMI select a PDCH if QoS was negotiated during PDP context activation?
The SwMI should choose whichever of its available PDCHs best suits the MS's QoS requirements, taking into account the QoS requirements of other MSs that are already using PDCHs in that cell.
What default assumption should the SwMI make if QoS was not negotiated during PDP context activation?
The SwMI should assume by default that the PDP context is required for background class data with unspecified throughput, delay and reliability.
What are the three main states defined for both the MS and SwMI in the SNDCP protocol?
The three main states are READY, STANDBY, and IDLE.
What does the READY state imply regarding the MS and packet data transfer?
The READY state implies that the MS is located on a PDCH and is currently engaged in packet data transfer or has recently been engaged in packet data transfer, as defined by a timer.
Under what condition does the SwMI direct the MS to leave the PDCH while in the READY state?
The SwMI directs the MS to leave the PDCH when the inactivity timer (the READY timer) expires in the MS or the SwMI.
What is the function of PDU priority and how can it affect transmission queuing and random access?

PDU priority consists of eight levels that allow the application to specify the PDU priority of a data packet. Data packets with high PDU priority may be queued for transmission ahead of those with lower PDU priority in the same MS. Additionally, the BS may restrict random access to the PDCH to higher PDU priorities, likely during times of heavy loading.
