Does direct mode equipment support power control, and how is uplink transmit power handled on DM repeaters?

Direct mode equipment does not support power control. However, when operated on DM repeaters, the transmitting MS may optionally control its uplink transmit power in a manner similar to trunked mode terminals.
What type of slot switching is required for direct mode MS-MS communications and for MSs operating with a repeater?
One slot switching is required for direct mode MS-MS communications and for MSs operating with a repeater.
How does the nomenclature for direct mode air interfaces in the Designers Guide Part 1 [i.13] differ from the one presented in this text?
In the Designers Guide Part 1 [i.13], Ud1 is called I6, Ud2 is called I6'', and Ud3 is called I6'.
What assumption is made regarding Talk Group membership for mobile stations in the operational examples?
It is assumed that all mobile stations are members of the same Talk Group, whether they are active in Direct Mode or Trunked Mode.
In the key for Figures 9 to 12, what does the line pattern '—— - - ——' denote?
It denotes transmissions initiated by active Trunk Mode mobile stations.
Besides circuit mode voice and data, what other types of communication can utilize the dual watch capability?
Dual watch capability can also be used to send and receive SDS messages and packet mode data, provided the destination mobile station is not busy in a call.
What specific address information must operational MSs know to use a Direct Mode Repeater?
Each operational MS allowed to use the repeater needs to know the 10 bit address identifying the repeater.
By what methods can an MS obtain the 10 bit address of a Direct Mode Repeater?
The address can be obtained by prior arrangement or by the DMO MS receiving the repeater presence signal containing the 10 bit address.
Why do MSs 2 and 3 ignore the set-up received directly from MS 1 in the described configuration?
They ignore it due to the inclusion of the Repeater address.
What is the primary function of a direct mode gateway in a TETRA network?
A direct mode gateway provides connectivity between a direct mode mobile station and the TETRA trunked network.
How does the direct mode gateway adjust timing and what is the benefit?
The direct mode gateway can make adjustments to the direct mode timing in order to avoid overlap with the trunked mode time slots, which reduces the physical requirements for the gateway.
What are the limitations regarding dual watch support during DMO gateway operation?

Dual watch on trunked mode is not supported when in DMO gateway operation. Similarly, dual watch on DMO is not supported when participating in a trunked mode gateway group call. This prevents an active MS from detecting individual or group calls on the other mode.
How can MS 1 be instructed to address the Repeater/Gateway when transmitting to the Talk Group?
MS 1 can be instructed by pre-programming, by selection, or by detection of the Repeater/Gateway presence signal.
What actions does the infrastructure take after the Repeater/Gateway forwards the set-up message from MS 1?

The infrastructure goes through the normal trunked mode group call set-up procedure and allocates a channel to the Talk Group, which includes MSs 3, 4, and 5 and also the gateway, when resources are available.
Why are up-link and down-link burst concepts not used in Direct Mode?
The concepts of up-link and down-link bursts are not used in Direct Mode because there is no infrastructure.
How are TDMA slots and frames structured in Direct Mode Operation (DMO)?
In DMO, four slots are grouped together to make a TDMA frame, and 18 frames are grouped to make a multi-frame.
Does Direct Mode Operation (DMO) support full duplex voice operation?
No, unlike trunked mode, DMO is not designed to support full duplex voice operation, even in individual calls.
What is the frequency requirement for Direct Mode Operation (DMO) compared to trunked mode?
Except for Type 1B and Type 2 repeaters plus Type 1B repeater gateways, DMO requires only a single frequency, not a duplex pair of frequencies.
Which slots are used for transmission and signalling in the simplest form of DMO?
In its simplest form, DMO operates on a single 25 kHz RF carrier with the active Tx mobile transmitting on slot 1, while slot 3 is used for other signalling.
Under what conditions is the MS-MS Normal Mode designed to be used?

It is designed for communication between DM-MSs when no base station is available (e.g., poor trunked mode coverage, overloaded or faulty infrastructure) or when users wish to bypass the infrastructure (e.g., for covert operation).
What is the primary purpose of direct mode repeaters (DM-REP)?
The purpose of all direct mode repeaters is to extend the coverage area of DM communications beyond that attained by MS-MS mode.
In which frames is the channel reservation signal carried for a reserved DM channel?
The channel reservation signal is carried in the DSBs in frames 6, 12, and 18.
Why is it desirable for all DM-MSs to understand the presence signal generated by a repeater?
If DM-MSs do not understand the presence signal, they could mistakenly interpret it as the channel being occupied when it is actually free.
How does the timing of the slave link relate to the master link in a system where the DM-REP re-transmits information?

The slave link lags the master link by three slots. For example, slave link frame 1 slot 1 coincides with master link frame 1 slot 4, and slave link frame 1 slot 2 coincides with master link frame 2 slot 1.
What distinguishes the RF carrier usage of a type 1B repeater from a type 1A repeater?
A type 1B repeater uses a pair of duplex-spaced RF carriers, with one serving as an uplink from DM-MSs to the DM-REP and the other as a downlink from the DM-REP to the DM-MSs.
How does the gateway handle information transfer between DM-MSs and the V+D system?
The gateway re-transmits information received from DM-MSs on the Ud3 air interface to the V+D system on the Um air interface and vice versa.
What are the consequences if the gateway does not inform the SwMI that it is a gateway?

If the gateway does not inform the SwMI that it is a gateway, the SwMI will see it as a normal V+D MS. Consequently, the gateway will only be able to support group calls, a single DM-MS, or individual calls from DM to V+D, but not individual calls from V+D to DM.
How does MS-MS frequency efficient mode achieve better use of the frequency spectrum?
It allows two DM channels per RF carrier, enabling two calls to take place simultaneously on the same RF carrier by using the two vacant timeslots in the TDMA frame structure for a second DM channel.
What are the names of the two DM channels in MS-MS frequency efficient mode and what synchronization requirement exists between them?

The two DM channels are referred to as channel A and channel B. Any call on channel B must be synchronized to the channel A call to maintain necessary slot timing alignment and prevent mutual interference.
How does the master MS on channel B acquire timing synchronization to minimize inter DM channel interference?
The master MS on channel B acquires its timing synchronization from channel A.
Why are MS-MS normal mode mobiles disadvantaged when operating on the same RF carrier as MS-MS frequency efficient mobiles?

MS-MS normal mode mobiles are disadvantaged because no pre-emption mechanism exists for them to pre-empt an MS-MS frequency efficient mode mobile to access the DM RF carrier, whereas they can pre-empt other normal mode mobiles.
What is required to obtain the full benefits of MS-MS frequency efficient mode operation?
The RF carrier should be devoted exclusively to MS-MS frequency efficient mode operation.
What is the frequency efficiency comparison between Repeater type 2 and Repeater type 1A?
Repeater type 2 has the same frequency efficiency as type 1A, meaning the efficiency of two calls on two RF carriers is the same as one call on one RF carrier.
What are the primary purposes of introducing a repeater in DM MS-MS communications?
The primary purposes of repeaters are to stabilize and extend the range of DM MS-MS communications.
What are the designations for single carrier and two carrier repeater systems?

The single carrier repeater was originally designated as type 1, and the two carrier repeater was designated as type 2. Later, the single carrier single call repeater was designated as type 1A, and the two carrier repeater supporting only one call at a time was designated as type 1B.
Why was the type 1B repeater introduced?
The type 1B repeater was introduced because implementing a type 2 repeater (which supports two calls) was not a trivial exercise. Type 1B uses two carriers but supports only one call at a time.
What is the maximum number of voice channels allowed per carrier pair in trunked mode and direct mode repeater respectively?
Trunked mode allows three voice channels per carrier pair, while a direct mode repeater allows a maximum of two.
What is one of the major criteria for selecting a DM repeater type?
One of the major criteria is to ensure co-existence with trunked mode base and mobile stations.
Which components could be affected by the TM-BS in the scenario of a type 1A DM-REP in the TM-BS transmit band?
The DM-MSs and the DM-REP could be affected by the TM-BS.
What are the potential interference paths when a direct mode group works through a type 1A DM-REP with the DM RF carrier in the base station receive band?
The TM-BS could be affected by the DM-MSs and the DM-REP, and the DM-MSs and the DM-REP could be affected by the TM-MSs.
Which figures illustrate the situation where a direct mode group operates through a type 1B or type 2 DM-REP with the transmitter in the TM-BS transmit band?
Figure 27 shows the situation, and Figure 28 shows the trunked mode and direct mode frequency utilization.
What are the four potential interference paths identified for a type 1B or type 2 DM-REP transmitter located in the TM-BS transmit band?
The TM-BS could be affected by the DM-MSs; the DM-MSs could be affected by the TM-BS; the DM-REP could be affected by the TM-MSs; and the TM-MSs could be affected by the DM-REP.
What is the recommended spatial relationship between TM-MSs and DM-REPs, and what is the impact on infrastructure if a type 1B or type 2 DM-REP is placed close to a trunked mode base station?

TM-MSs should not be used close to DM-REPs and vice versa. However, this configuration has the least adverse impact on the trunked mode infrastructure if the type 1B or type 2 DM-REP/GATE were inadvertently placed close to a trunked mode base station.
What operational restriction applies to the arrangement of co-located DM-REP and TM-MSs regarding proximity to a TM-BS?
Care should be taken that this arrangement does not operate close to a TM-BS.
Why should the configuration with a DM-REP transmitter in the TM-BS receive band not be used for a mobile trunked mode base station?
This configuration should not be used for a mobile trunked mode base station because the frequencies are the reverse of normal trunked mode.
Which four potential interference paths are identified in the frequency configuration where the DM-REP transmit RF carrier is in the base station receive band?

The potential interference paths are: the TM-BS could be affected by the DM-REP; the DM-REP could be affected by the TM-BS; the DM-MSs could be affected by the TM-MSs; and the TM-MSs could be affected by the DM-MSs.
Which equipment is particularly susceptible to interference when DM-REP and DM-MSs are far from TM-BS but close to TM-MSs, and why?
TM-MSs are particularly susceptible because the signal level from the TM-BS will be low.
What are the interference effects of using DM-REP type 1A in the TM-BS transmit band versus the receive band?

DM-REP type 1A in the TM-BS transmit band causes no interference to DM terminals, but TM-MSs within the stay-away distance are affected. DM-REP type 1A in the TM-BS receive band causes no interference to TM-BS or TM-MSs, but DM terminals within the stay-away distance are affected by TM-MSs.
What is the consequence of a DM-REP type 1B transmitter operating in the TM-BS transmit band?
It will result in the TM-MSs and the DM-REP interfering.
Why is the TM-BS particularly susceptible to interference when DM terminals operate close to it?
The TM-BS is particularly susceptible because it could always be trying to receive the low signal level from a distant TM-MS.
What is the only solution that prevents interference from reducing the range of the TM-BS?
DM-REP type 1A in TM-BS transmit band.
What stay-away distance is recommended if the trunked mode BS is to be little affected by the direct mode equipment?
Up to 110 m, depending on the BS transmitter power and frequency separation between DM and TM.
How do MSs detect when an RF carrier is occupied by another group in MS-MS mode or with type 1A repeaters?
All the MSs monitor the same RF carrier and detect when it is occupied by another group.
Why is it recommended that the DM-REP not be configured to transmit its presence signal on a free channel?

Because the DM-REP will not be able to detect the MS-MS MSs, so if it is configured to transmit its presence signal when it considers the channel to be free, it could interfere with an MS-MS call in progress.
What is dual watch operation?

Dual watch operation is the underlying feature that allows a suitably enabled MS to keep track of calls addressed to its individual identity (ITSI) or one of its Group Identities (GTSIs) on both the trunked and direct mode nets.
What are the operational capabilities of a Dual Watch mobile station (DW-MS) in full dual watch mode?

In full dual watch, a DW-MS is capable of monitoring the Trunked Mode control channel while active in Direct Mode, or monitoring a Direct Mode channel while active in Trunked Mode. The MS can only be active in one mode at a given time.
Under what conditions can a DW-MS perform idle dual watch?
In idle dual watch, the MS can only dual watch on the other mode when it is not active in either trunked or direct mode.
How does Frequency efficient mode affect timing adjustments for Dual Watch operations?
Frequency efficient mode does not support timing changes. If a DO-MS initiates a call with unsuitable timing, any DW-MSs participating in the call will have to revert to idle dual watch.
How does an MS in full dual watch manage energy on the Trunked Mode control channel?
It uses energy economy mechanisms to ensure that the MS listens at negotiated times to the TMO.
What criteria does the TETRA DMO standard define for a dual watching MS to select an incoming call?
The selection is based only on priority and addressing.
What is the purpose of channel surveillance performed by a DM-MS while tuned to an RF carrier?
The purpose is to determine the state of the channel before initiating a call and to detect incoming calls that may be addressed to the MS.
How does a DM-MS perceive the state of a DM channel?
A DM channel is perceived by a DM-MS as being free, occupied, or reserved.
Under what condition is a DM RF carrier considered available?
A DM RF carrier is available when there is no direct mode activity detected on that channel above the Rx sensitivity level.
What factors influence the degree of energy efficiency achievable in DMO, and how does this affect MSs from different manufacturers?

The degree of energy efficiency depends on many factors, such as the number of DSBs the receiver requires to see to obtain the necessary synchronization information. Consequently, MSs from different manufacturers may vary in their battery economy performance.
How does a DM-MS authenticate itself in dual-watch mode?
In dual-watch mode, a DM-MS authenticates itself to the TETRA V+D network using the procedures for V+D operation.
How does the RF carrier configuration for the DM-MS differ in direct mode operation compared to trunked mode?
In direct mode operation, the transmitter and receiver of the DM-MS are on the same RF carrier.
Where can the direct mode RF carrier assignment be placed relative to the trunked mode band?
It can be placed anywhere: within the same band as used for trunked mode, outside it, or between the BS transmit and receive segments.
What characteristic of the TETRA modulation scheme allows direct mode systems to be implemented within the trunked mode band?
The modulation scheme employed by TETRA is sufficiently robust to permit direct mode systems to be implemented within the trunked mode band.
How are the maximum levels of transmitter noise expressed in the TETRA specification?
The maximum levels of transmitter noise are expressed relative to the power of the transmitter rather than as absolute levels.
How is the term frb defined in the context of V+D base station bands?
frb is defined as the frequency offset between the edge of the V+D base station receive band and the near edge of the V+D base station transmit band.
How do unwanted wideband transmitter noise and blocking signals affect the effective range of a receiver?
They produce noise in the receiver on the wanted channel, which drowns out wanted signals at the maximum range, thereby reducing the effective range of the receiver.
What are the assumed values for the receiver noise floor (NF) and additional path loss (LA) for mobile stations?
For mobile stations, the assumed receiver noise floor (NF) is -122 dBm, and the additional path loss (LA) is 14 dB.
What receiver noise floor (NF) value is recommended for a base station, and why does it differ from mobile stations?
It is recommended that the receiver noise floor (NF) for a base station be assumed to be -125 dBm because a base station is more sensitive than a mobile station.
How does the path loss requirement for unwanted noise compare to that for blocking across all frequency separations and classes of MS?
In all cases, the path loss for unwanted noise is greater than that for blocking.
How do the effects on stay-away distance change with increasing class of MS and increasing frequency separation?
The effects increase with increasing class of MS (i.e. with increasing MS power) and decrease with increasing frequency separation.
Under what condition might the assumption of an additional loss term of LA = 14 dB no longer hold?
The assumption of an additional loss term of LA = 14 dB may well no longer hold if the victim receiver is not a hand-held MS, such as a vehicle mounted MS.
Why does the assumed noise floor of the receiver depend on whether it is a mobile station or a base station under the TETRA specification?
Because under the TETRA specification, MS and base stations have different reference sensitivities.
Why is placing direct mode frequencies in the base station transmit band considered the preferred configuration?

It is the preferred configuration because trunked mode operation will be least affected if direct mode MS operates close to a base station, reducing interference effects by avoiding TMO BS receiver blocking.
What risks are associated with placing direct mode MS-MS frequencies in the base station receive band?

This configuration should be used with care because DM MSs operating close to the trunked mode BS may cause severe desensitization. Additionally, direct mode MSs could suffer blocking and desensitization from trunked mode MS transmissions, and their transmissions could cause problems for trunked mode base stations.
Which devices are transmitting on close frequencies when direct mode frequencies are placed in the base station receive band?
Both the trunked mode and direct mode MSs are transmitting close to the same frequencies.
What is the difference in impact between reducing the range of nearby trunked mode MSs and reducing the range of a base station?

Reducing the range of nearby trunked mode MSs will probably affect one or two users, while reducing the range of a base station could potentially affect many users on that base station, which would be a more serious problem.
What frequency separation is required to achieve a 5 m stay-away distance between DMO MS-MSs, based on field trials considering non-linear blocking?
A frequency separation of 50 kHz between wanted and unwanted signals is required.
Under what conditions does a repeater send a presence signal?

The repeater sends the presence signal during calls. It can also optionally send it when it detects that the channel is free to indicate its presence to the MSs, depending on the group's operational procedures.
How should the first MSs arriving at an incident communicate if the repeater has not yet arrived?

The first MSs should begin communicating amongst themselves using DM MS-MS normal mode, as frequency efficient mode is not valid for operation with a type 1 repeater. They should be organized in one or more talkgroups on the same channel, where receiving MSs (slaves) synchronize to the transmitting MS (master).
What can MSs do if they arrive at a designated channel that is free?
If the channel is free, MSs can either listen for the next call or initiate one.
Why is it preferable to configure a type 1A repeater to send its presence signal when the channel is free?

It is preferable because if an MS initiates a call in MS-MS normal mode while the repeater is operational, the standard does not define whether other MSs will accept the call, even though they receive it. Sending the presence signal ensures MSs know the repeater is operating.
Who determines how MSs switch from MS-MS normal mode to repeater mode?
The method for switching from MS-MS normal to repeater mode is not defined in the standard; it is determined by the manufacturer with user input and may be carried out manually by the user.
How does the geometric definition of the communication group change when a repeater is used compared to direct MS-to-MS communication?
Without a repeater, the diameter of the group is limited to the MS to MS range. With a repeater at the centre or in a location with height gain, the MS to MS range becomes the radius of the group.
Why might the actual increase in reliable communication area be less than quadruple when using a repeater, and how is this reduction minimized?

The increase could be less than quadruple because every transmission path now has two legs. This reduction is minimized because the repeater de-encodes and re-encodes the MS transmissions before forwarding them, which improves the bit error performance.
What should the DM-MS do to attach to the GTSIs of the trunked network?
The DM-MS should attach to the GTSIs of the trunked network via the DM-GATE following the procedures defined in EN 300 396-5 [i.5].
Why does a repeater alone fail to satisfy operational requirements in the DMO range extension scenario with link into TMO?
The repeater alone would not provide connectivity back to the trunked infrastructure.
Under what condition can MSs communicate in MS-MS normal mode before the helicopter arrives?
MSs can communicate in MS-MS normal mode before the helicopter arrives provided that they are not obscured from each other by the cliff.
What factors determine how MSs switch to repeater/gateway operation when a helicopter arrives with a REP/GATE?
The switching method depends on whether MS-to-MS communications are on the DM-REP/GATE uplink or downlink frequency, and whether the DM-REP/GATE transmits its presence signal on the free channel.
If the uplink frequency is used for MS-to-MS communications, how should MSs be instructed to switch to repeater/gateway operation?
Since MSs will not detect the presence signal on the downlink frequency, they need to be told to switch by a call on the downlink frequency, preferably from the helicopter.
What facility should the repeater/gateway have if the downlink frequency is used for transmission?
The repeater/gateway should preferably have the facility to monitor activity on its downlink frequency to avoid starting to transmit its presence signal while an MS-to-MS call is taking place.
Why can the cliff top MS and cliff foot MS not communicate directly or via the helicopter in gateway operation?
In gateway operation, communication is from the transmitting MS direct to the receiving MSs.
What action should officers take if they are in areas inside a building with no repeater coverage?

Officers should switch their MSs to the direct MS-MS frequency. This relies on another MS in the vicinity also being switched, which can be coordinated via a visible signal since officers in hazardous areas are assumed to be within sight of at least one other officer.
Which assumption regarding the receiver cannot be directly checked according to ETSI TR 102 300-3 V1.3.3?
The linearity of the receiver is the only assumption that cannot be directly checked.
Why are no stay-away distances provided for frequency separations of 75 kHz and 250 kHz?

No stay-away distances are given for 75 kHz and 250 kHz because the ACP and ACR figures are taken from the TETRA DMO standard in bands. Consequently, the figures for 75 kHz are the same as those for 50 kHz, and the figures for 250 kHz are the same as those for 100 kHz.
Under what conditions will blocking dominate due to non-linear responses in the receiver?
Blocking will dominate if the incident noise (unwanted signal) is greater than -25 dBm for adjacent channel scenarios, or greater than -5 dBm for other blocking effects.
What signal level thresholds are used to calculate the "non-linear" stay-away distance for adjacent channel and other cases?
The unwanted signal must fall below -25 dBm for the adjacent channel case and below -5 dBm otherwise.
What is the primary cause of signal degradation for an MS when the wanted signal is not weak?
The prime cause is likely to be blocking, rather than unwanted adjacent power or noise emitted from the interfering MS.
What DMO frequency separations are required in rural and urban areas to achieve a stay-away distance of less than 5 m?
A DMO frequency separation of 50 kHz should be maintained in rural areas and 100 kHz in urban areas.
What was the addressing concept in traditional PMR?

Traditional PMR had no concept of addressing. There was a type of individual addressing in the form of call signs that speakers were required to identify themselves by on the channel, but it was by no means selective addressing.
How does TETRA trunked mode manage call control for the user?

TETRA trunked mode has a fully automatic call control protocol. The control system of the MS first searches for the control channel, communicates with the BS to gain service and then manages the service on behalf of the user.
Why are the implementations described in the TETRA direct mode standards annex considered only examples?
The DMO standard has been drafted with great flexibility, allowing manufacturers to offer other implementations that may more closely match users' precise requirements.
Why is it unlikely that DMO will be available for free standing operation despite not being precluded by the ETSI standard?
Due to expected national licensing constraints.
Under what conditions does TETRA numbering become more challenging?

Numbering becomes more challenging if a Private Numbering Plan (PNP) is laid on top of the basic TETRA numbering scheme and if this PNP is to be made compatible with a corporate PABX or national PSTN numbering scheme.
Why might each DM-MS need to know the address of repeaters and gateways in advance?
To prevent much RF channel capacity from being used by DM-MSs attempting access on the wrong repeaters and gateways, especially when access is limited.
Besides their own identity, what identities may repeaters and gateways broadcast?
Repeaters and gateways may broadcast TETRA Subscriber Identities (TSIs), which can be individual or group addresses allowed access.
How does broadcasting an organization-wide group identity facilitate access for members of that organization?
Broadcasting the group identity enables access from all members of the organization, even if they are making individual calls or calls to different group numbers.
What is the purpose of the channel surveillance mechanism in MS-MS direct mode?
The channel surveillance mechanism is designed to control access to the channel to prevent transmission over an ongoing call, while still allowing access in emergency situations.
What distinguishes MS-MS normal mode from MS-MS frequency efficient mode regarding DM channels on a carrier?
In MS-MS normal mode, only one DM channel may exist on a DM RF carrier, whereas in MS-MS frequency efficient mode, two DM channels (designated channel A and channel B) may exist on a DM RF carrier.
In TETRA DMO, how is synchronization achieved between MSs in the absence of a base station?
The master DM-MS provides the timing and frequency synchronization for the channel. Any slave DM-MS may request a timing change, usually because it is dual watching.
Which Protocol Data Unit abbreviation represents DM-CONNECT and in which burst type is it sent?
The abbreviation 'cn' represents DM-CONNECT, and it is sent in DSB.
What is the difference in transmission burst type between DM-PRE ACCEPT and the combination of DM-PRE ACCEPT + DM-RELEASE?
DM-PRE ACCEPT (pa) is sent in DSB, whereas DM-PRE ACCEPT + DM-RELEASE (par) is sent in DNB.
What are the essential building blocks of the DMO structure and their composition?
The essential building blocks are the frame, which comprises four timeslots, and the multiframe, which comprises 18 frames.
Which frames carry reservation information in DSBs in slots 1 and 3?
Frames 6 and 12 carry reservation information in DSBs in slots 1 and 3.
In which frames and slot is pre-emption permitted during occupation?
Pre-emption is permitted in slot 3 of frames 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, and 17.
What are the two main purposes of the channel surveillance monitoring process in direct mode?
It enables the MS to detect calls addressed to it and permits the MS to know if other users are on the channel when its user wishes to make a call.
In which frames do the synchronization bursts denoting channel occupation occur following initial synchronization?
The synchronization bursts denoting occupation of the channel occur in slot 3 of frames 6, 12, and 18 following the initial synchronization.
Why is actual speech unlikely to be available immediately after pressing the PTT in TETRA systems?
Actual speech is unlikely to be available immediately because there is generally a delay between pressing the PTT and speaking, and the TETRA codec requires processing time to prepare the speech.
What is the purpose of the late entry feature in TETRA direct mode?
Late entry permits a mobile station (MS) that missed the initial call set-up messages to enter a call while it is still in progress.
How are occupation messages transmitted to enable late entry in TETRA direct mode?
Occupation messages are sent using DSBs in slot 3 of frames 6, 12, and 18, and also in slot 1 of frame 18.
For which type of calls is late entry generally applicable in TETRA direct mode?
Late entry is generally only applicable for calls set up without presence check, as these calls proceed without an acknowledgement from the called DM-MS.
What is the term for the procedure of terminating one call transaction and starting another during a TETRA direct mode call?
The procedure is termed changeover.
What is the purpose of the reservation messages sent by the master MS during the reservation period, and how are they transmitted?

The reservation messages inform other idle MSs on the channel that the call is not necessarily finished and may restart with another speaker, preventing other user groups from setting up their own calls during a momentary break. The master MS sends these messages using DSBs in slots 1 and 3 of frames 6, 12, and 18.
What action does the requester take upon receiving a changeover acknowledgement?

The requester transmits a sequence of set-up messages in synchronization bursts ("su"). This action effects the call changeover, with the requester becoming the new master for the next call transaction.
How does the master handle simultaneous changeover requests from slave DM-MSs that cause interference?

The master receives no clear request and maintains the channel in reservation mode, transmitting reservation signalling when appropriate. This continues until another changeover request is successfully received or the reservation timer times out and the channel is released totally.
What is the purpose of the channel reservation mechanism?
The channel reservation mechanism ensures an orderly use of the channel by giving a degree of priority to the existing call.
What mechanism allows the current transmitting MS to be interrupted in Direct mode?
The mechanism is known as pre-emption.
What message does a DM-MS transmit to perform pre-emption?
The DM-MS transmits a pre-emption request message, denoted as "prq".
What actions does the master take after successfully decoding a valid pre-emption request?

The master announces that the channel has been pre-empted to both the pre-empting DM-MS and the other DM-MSs involved in the ongoing call by means of the pre-emption acknowledgement message. Upon issuing this message, the master ceases its role and relinquishes the channel.
How does the successful pre-emptor proceed after the master relinquishes the channel during pre-emption?
The successful pre-emptor transmits set-up messages for the new call with a new group or individual addressee and becomes the master for the initial transaction of this new call.
What initial actions does a DM-MS take after finding a channel free to establish synchronization and its role as master?
The DM-MS linearizes its transmitter, establishes channel synchronization, and assumes the role of 'master' by transmitting a sequence of DM-SDS UDATA message headers using the DSB structure.
How are the remaining parts of a short data message transmitted by the master DM-MS after the initial headers?
The remaining parts are transmitted without repetition using the DNB structure in slot 1 of the following frames.
Under what conditions and how may a master DM-MS repeat a complete message transmission for reliability?
For reliability, the master DM-MS may repeat the complete message transmission immediately without re-checking that the channel is free, starting again with DSBs.
Where is pre-emption signalling permitted during an SDS transmission involving DNBs?
Short data occupation DSBs are sent in slot 3 of frames 6, 12, and 18 during the transmission of the DNBs.
What structure and repetition method does the master DM-MS use to transmit the remaining parts of a short data message?
The master DM-MS transmits the remaining parts of the short data message without repetition and using the DNB structure, in slot 1 of the following frames.
When does the receiving slave DM-MS send an acknowledgement to the master DM-MS?
The receiving slave DM-MS sends an acknowledgement to the master DM-MS following the receipt of the last burst containing data.
What are the three types of DM-MS defined in the text?
The three types of DM-MS are DO-MS (direct mode only), DU-MS (dual mode), and DW-MS (dual watch).
What capabilities must a DM-MS possess to operate correctly?

To operate correctly, a DM-MS must know which groups it is a member of, know which priority levels it can use, and be capable of at least one of circuit mode speech, circuit mode data, or short data service.
Which entity provides frequency synchronization and which provides timing synchronization in repeater type 1A operation?
Frequency synchronization is provided by the DM-REP, while timing synchronization is provided by the master DM-MS.
What is the synchronization chain for slave DM-MSs in repeater type 1A operation?
The DM-REP synchronizes its timing to the master DM-MS, and the slave DM-MSs then synchronize their timing to the DM-REP.
In which slots and frames of the slave link is pre-emption signalling permitted during occupation for a type 1A repeater?
Pre-emption signalling is permitted during occupation in slot 3 of slave link frames 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, and 17.
How does the DM-REP re-transmit a pre-emption message to the current master DM-MS after detecting it on the slave link?
The DM-REP re-transmits the pre-emption message to the current master DM-MS in slot 3 of master link frame 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, or 1 respectively.
Which master link frames may carry a DM-REP presence signal in a DSB in slot 3?
Frames 1, 7, and 13 of the master link may carry a DM-REP presence signal in a DSB in slot 3.
When does an operational repeater send its presence signal?

An operational repeater sends its presence signal when it is forwarding a call and optionally when the channel is free, allowing MSs monitoring the channel to inform their users that the repeater is available.
How does the master DM-MS establish its role and synchronize the channel?

It transmits a sequence of call set-up messages on the master link using the DSB structure as given in EN 300 396-2, clause 9.4.3. These messages are sent in an appropriate number of frames and contain frame count information defining their position in the 18-frame cyclic multiframe structure.
Why does the master DM-MS listen for synchronization bursts re-transmitted by the DM-REP?
To confirm that its signalling to the DM-REP was successful.
Which structure is used by the master DM-MS to transmit traffic, and when does this transmission occur in the provided example?
The master DM-MS uses the DNB structure, as given in EN 300 396-2, clause 9.4.3. In the example, it transmits traffic in the next available frame, which is frame 3 of the master link.
What is the role of the synchronization burst in a type 1 DM-REP set-up with presence check?
The synchronization burst requests a response indicating the presence of the DM-MS which has been addressed as the recipient in the set-up attempt.
Describe the transmission timing of the connect message by the slave DM-MS in the provided example.

In the example, the slave linearizes its transmitter in slot 1 of frame 2 of the slave link, sends a connect message in slot 3 of this frame, and then repeats the connect message in the following frame.
When does a requesting DM-MS send the changeover request message ("txr") in the described example?
The changeover request message ("txr") is sent by a requesting DM-MS in the next available slot 3 on the slave link following reception of the txc'.
What happens to the master's role and responsibility after transmitting changeover acknowledgement messages ("txa") on the master link?
After transmitting the changeover acknowledgement messages on the master link, the master becomes a slave and has no further responsibility for the channel.
What action does the requester take upon receiving the repeated changeover acknowledgement message (txa')?
The requester transmits a sequence of set-up messages in synchronization bursts on the master link, using the same frame and slot timing as the previous master.
In the example illustrated in figure E.11, when would the first traffic burst of the new master take place?
The first traffic burst of the new master would take place in frame 4 on the master link.
Why might MS designers consider means to alleviate operational effects of delays when operating with a DM-REP?
Because the procedure for changeover when operating with a DM-REP takes longer than for direct MS-MS operation.
In which specific slots and frames of the slave link is pre-emption allowed during occupation?
Pre-emption is allowed only in slot 3 of slave link frames 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, and 17.
How does the master announce that a channel has been pre-empted after decoding a valid request?

The master announces the pre-emption by sending a pre-emption acknowledgement message ("par" and "pa") on the master link, which is subsequently repeated on the slave link. This announcement is made to both the pre-empting DM-MS and the other DM-MSs involved in the ongoing call.
What steps must a DM-MS take to send an unacknowledged short data message through a type 1 DM-REP when the channel is free?

The DM-MS must linearize its transmitter, establish channel synchronization, and simultaneously establish its role as 'master' by transmitting a sequence of DM-SDS UDATA message headers on the master link using the DSB structure.
How many synchronization bursts are sent in the example where they are transmitted in 2 frames?
A total of 8 bursts.
Which types of DM-MS can be used with a DM-REP and what configuration is required?

All three types of DM-MS (DO-MS direct mode only, DU-MS dual mode, and DW-MS dual watch) can be used with a DM-REP. They must be configured with additional protocols to enable operation with a DM-REP.
What actions must a DM-MS take regarding the DM-REP presence signal?
The DM-MS needs to recognize the DM-REP presence signal and read its type and address.
What procedure must a DM-MS have for mode switching when operating with a DM-REP?
The DM-MS must have a procedure for switching from MS-MS mode to repeater mode.
Why is it recommended for a DM-REP to send its presence signal at irregular intervals?
It is recommended to send the signal at irregular intervals to avoid repeated collisions if other DM-REPs or gateways are trying to use the channel.
What is the major difference between a type 1B repeater and a type 1A repeater?
The major difference is that the type 1B repeater's downlink and uplink channels are on different frequencies.
How many DM channels can exist on a pair of DM RF carriers during type 1B repeater operation?
Only one DM channel may exist on a pair of DM RF carriers.
How is frequency synchronization achieved in type 1B DM repeater operation?
Frequency synchronization is provided by the DM-REP. The DM-MSs align their frequency with the DM-REP's downlink carrier and use that reference when transmitting on the uplink carrier.
How is timing synchronization established among the DM-REP, master DM-MS, and slave DM-MSs?
Timing synchronization is provided by the master DM-MS. The DM-REP synchronizes its timing to the master DM-MS, and the slave DM-MSs then synchronize their timing to the DM-REP.
How does the protocol stack for DM-GATE operation differ from that of MS-MS and repeater operation?

The protocol stack for DM-GATE operation is the same as for MS-MS and repeater operation, with the addition of a Direct Mode Mobility Management (DMMM) entity to support the additional optional procedure of registration.
How many DM channels may exist on one DM RF carrier during gateway operation?
With gateway operation, only one DM channel may exist on one DM RF carrier.
What are the frequency interface requirements for a gateway in DM-MS operation?
The gateway operates on a single carrier frequency on the DM air interface and on a frequency pair on the V+D interface.
Which frames of the master link may carry a DM-GATE presence signal in a DSB in slot 3?
Frames 1, 7, and 13 of the master link may carry a DM-GATE presence signal in a DSB in slot 3.
What is the slot lag of the DM channel relative to the V+D downlink slot 1 of the main carrier?
The DM channel lags the V+D downlink slot 1 of the main carrier by 3 slots.
Why is the original 3-slot lag from the signalling phase maintained during traffic channel allocation?
The original 3-slot lag is maintained because it imposes the minimum requirements on the gateway's physical layer and avoids the need for the gateway to store and forward a burst of traffic.
What is the delay incurred in relaying traffic from the V+D MS to the DM channel?
The delay is 5 slots.
In which specific slots and frames do synchronization bursts denoting occupation of the DM channel occur following initial synchronization?
They occur in slot 3 of frames 6 and 12, and in slots 1 and 3 of frame 18.
What is the basic philosophy of the message sequence for a request originating from a DM-MS?
It comprises the request, an optional interim acknowledge, and then a final acknowledgement (or rejection).
What changes occur in roles and actions after the gateway receives the D-CONNECT message from the SwMI?
On receipt of the D-CONNECT, the gateway sends DM-GCONNECT to the calling DM-MS. The calling DM-MS then assumes the role of master and begins the normal DM call set-up followed by traffic.
What decision does the gateway make after successfully decoding the first set-up burst from the DM-MS?
The gateway decides whether to send the DM-GACK interim acknowledgement to the calling DM-MS before sending the call request to the SwMI.
How does the SwMI respond when resources are immediately available, and what does it demand from the gateway?

The SwMI responds by sending D-SETUP and D-CONNECT messages to the V+D group members and gateway respectively in the same slot. It demands a layer 2 acknowledgement from the gateway in a reserved subslot on the allocated traffic channel, slot 3.
What actions does the DM-MS take after receiving the DM-GCONNECT message from the gateway?
The DM-MS assumes the role of master, follows the new timing established by the gateway, generates DM-SETUP messages on the DM channel to alert group members, and then proceeds to send its traffic.
How does frame 18 alignment affect gateway storage requirements for traffic flowing between the V+D and DM channels?

For traffic flowing from the V+D channel to the DM channel, the frame 18 alignment means there is no need for the gateway to store a burst of traffic. However, for traffic flowing from the DM channel to the V+D channel, the gateway is required to store one burst of traffic across the frame 18 boundary.
Why must the gateway store and delay the relay of traffic burst tc2 sent in slot 1 of frame 17 on the DM channel?

The traffic burst tc2 cannot be relayed as usual 3 slots later on the V+D uplink because that timing lies inside a frame 18. Consequently, the gateway is forced to store the traffic burst and relay it in the next available frame, which is frame 1.
What is the recommended approach for frame numbering during change-over?
It is recommended that the frame numbering remain consistent with change-over and that the numbering be chosen initially with the DM channel numbering lagging that of the V+D downlink.
When are synchronization bursts denoting occupation of the DM channel transmitted following initial synchronization?
Following initial synchronization, synchronization bursts denoting occupation of the DM channel occur in slot 3 of frames 6 and 12, and in slots 1 and 3 of frame 18.
What messages does the SwMI use to allocate a traffic channel after receiving a U-CONNECT from the gateway?
The SwMI allocates a traffic channel using the D-CONNECT and D-CONNECT ACKNOWLEDGE messages.
What sequence of actions does the gateway perform after receiving the D-CONNECT ACKNOWLEDGE?
After receiving the D-CONNECT ACKNOWLEDGE, the gateway sends DM-CONNECT ACK to the called DM-MS to enable it to prepare for receipt of traffic, and then forwards the traffic received from the SwMI.
How does the DM-GCONNECT message affect slot numbering and what does the gateway send to the SwMI while waiting for the DM-MS?

The DM-GCONNECT message redefines slot numbering as necessary for alignment with the V+D channel; in the example, it delays slot numbering by two slots to maintain a 3-slot lag. The gateway also sends null PDUs to the SwMI until the calling DM-MS is ready to send traffic.
What messages does the requesting DM-MS transmit after receiving changeover acknowledgement messages?
The requesting DM-MS transmits a sequence of set-up messages as master ('su').
What does the gateway send after receiving the transmission grant from the SwMI but before receiving traffic from the V+D MS uplink?
The gateway sends null PDUs until traffic is received from the V+D MS uplink.
How does a DM-MS effect pre-emption of a V+D MS, and how does the gateway respond if the request is valid?

To effect pre-emption, the DM-MS sends a DM-GPREEMPT message. If the gateway successfully decodes it as a valid request, it sends a transmission demand to the SwMI using a U-TX DEMAND PDU with the priority set appropriately.
In which specific slots and frames is pre-emption allowed during occupation?
During occupation, pre-emption is allowed only in slot 3 of frames 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, and 17.
When does the gateway send the U-TX DEMAND message to the SwMI after receiving a pre-emption request, and why is this timing chosen?

The gateway sends the U-TX DEMAND message to the SwMI in slot 3 of frame 7 on the V+D uplink. This is the first possible frame because slot 3 of frame 6 would not have allowed sufficient time to decode the pre-emption request received in the preceding slot.
How does the gateway inform the pre-empting DM-MS that transmit permission has been granted, and how is reliability increased for this message?

The gateway informs the pre-empting DM-MS using the DM-GPRE ACCEPT message, sent in the traffic slots (slot 1) of frames 8 and 9 on the DM channel along with a DM-TX CEASED message. Reliability is increased by repeating the DM-GPRE ACCEPT message in slot 3 of both frames.
What action does the requesting DM-MS take upon receipt of acknowledgement messages in the pre-emption timing diagram?
The requesting DM-MS transmits a sequence of set-up messages as master ('su').
What information does the DMAC-SYNC PDU sent by the DM-MS contain?

The DMAC-SYNC PDU specifies that the call is via a DM-GATE and contains the DM-GATE address, the source address (the DM-MS's ISSI, either real or pseudo), the destination address of the called individual or group and all the information needed by the called party to process the message, including encryption keys.
How are frequency and timing synchronization handled in Type 1A DM-REP/GATE operation, and what happens if a DM-MS has not received recent signals?

Frequency and timing synchronization are provided by the DM-REP/GATE. If a DM-MS has not received signals from the DM-REP/GATE sufficiently recently, it chooses an arbitrary timing. The DM-REP/GATE can then announce a modification of the timing, and the DM-MS will align its timing to the DM-REP/GATE.
What does an abbreviation with a prime symbol (') indicate in the slot timing diagrams for DM-REP/GATE operation?
An abbreviation with a (') indicates a repeated transmission sent by the repeater, on either the master link or the slave link.
What impact does a type 1B DM-REP/GATE offering a type 2 DM-REP function have on DM-MS gateway operation?
Since there is no procedure for a DM-MS to pre-empt a type 2 call to make a normal mode call, using this option will stop DM-MSs from using gateway operation until the type 2 call(s) have ended.
How many DM channels can exist on a pair of DM RF carriers during type 1B DM-REP/GATE operation?
Only one DM channel may exist on a pair of DM RF carriers.
How do DM-MSs handle frequency and timing synchronization with a DM-REP/GATE?

Frequency and timing synchronization are provided by the DM-REP/GATE. DM-MSs align their frequency with the DM-REP/GATE's downlink carrier and use that reference when transmitting on the uplink carrier. If signals have not been received sufficiently recently, the DM-MS chooses an arbitrary timing, and the DM-REP/GATE can announce a timing modification for the DM-MS to align to.
How must a DM-MS know the uplink and downlink frequencies for configuration?
The DM-MS needs to know the uplink and downlink frequencies, either by prior knowledge or from the gateway presence signal.
What capability does frequency efficient mode provide in addition to basic DM functionality?
Frequency efficient mode offers a method whereby two calls can take place simultaneously on the same RF carrier.
Which device provides timing synchronization for both channel A and channel B under normal operation?
The channel A master DM-MS provides the timing synchronization for both the A and B channels.
Which timeslots do not send DSBs for message repetition in MS-MS frequency efficient mode?
DSBs are not sent in timeslots 2 and 4 for the message repetition.
What synchronization roles do the channel A master DM-MS and the DM-REP perform for channels A and B?
The channel A master DM-MS provides the timing synchronization for both the A and B channels, while the DM-REP provides the frequency synchronization for both channels.
Under what condition could a DM-REP choose to start re-transmission sooner than after the end of the master DM-MS's set-up messages?
If the DM-REP had received one of the first of the master DM-MS's set-up messages, it could have chosen to start the re-transmission sooner.
What is the benefit of the DM-REP starting re-transmission sooner upon receiving initial set-up messages?
It allows the DM-REP to indicate as soon as possible that channel A had become busy, thereby preventing other DM-MSs from sending colliding set-up signalling.
When a pre-emption request is made in slot 3 of frame 3 on the slave link, when and where is it re-transmitted on the master link?
It is re-transmitted 4 slots later in slot 3 of frame 5 on the master link.
What action does the channel B master DM-MS take after the type 2 DM-REP repeats the set-up messages on the slave link?
The channel B master DM-MS monitors the downlink for the repeat transmissions and sends its traffic after the completion of the transmission of these messages.
How does the DM-REP handle the master's set-up messages in MS-MS operation?
The repeater re-sends the master's set-up messages on the slave link.
In which slots are the set-up messages sent by the new master in frames 18 and 1 of the master link transmitted?
The set-up messages are sent only in slots 1 and 3 and not slots 2 and 4.
In which slots and frames of the slave link is pre-emption allowed during occupation?
Pre-emption is allowed only in slot 3 of slave link frames 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 and 18.
When do traffic transmissions begin on the master link after a successful pre-emption?
Traffic transmissions begin in slot 1 of frame 4 on the master link.
Why does the master DM-MS not use slots 2 and 4 when transmitting the remaining parts of the short data message?
The master DM-MS does not use slots 2 and 4 in case the other DM channel may now be in use.
Under what condition may the DM-REP choose to use slots 2 and 4 when repeating messages on the slave link?
The DM-REP may choose to use slots 2 and 4 when it repeats the messages on the slave link if the other DM channel is not in use.
How does DM-REP transmit to ensure enhanced reliability?
DM-REP transmits in all 4 slots in each frame.
How are advanced features of DMR radios enabled in Smart MDM?
The user needs to apply for a license for advanced features and then enable the features by importing the license.
中继模式的主要功能是什么？使用该模式有什么前提条件？
中继模式下，终端作为网关，将接收到的专网语音或公网语音在专网和公网之间相互转发。该模式需授权后才可使用。
在中继模式下操作专网界面时，关于通过方向键选择区域有什么限制？
在中继模式下的专网待机界面，不能通过按【上移】/【下移】方向键选择区域。
图标DD、EE、SS和AA分别对应开启了哪些功能？
DD表示已开启监听功能，EE表示已开启扰频功能，SS表示已开启静噪功能，AA表示已开启紧急呼叫。
该设备的无线数据通信支持哪些GSM频段？
在“新建会话属性”窗口中，协议应选择什么？
SFTP
报警发起的紧急呼叫在集群业务中具有什么优先级及资源分配特性？
报警发起的紧急呼叫在所有集群业务中具有最高优先级，可以优先分配资源，甚至抢占其他业务的资源。
紧急告警功能通过什么方式实现，其优先级表现如何？
紧急告警功能是通过发送特定的紧急告警状态消息来实现的。该业务具有很高优先级，可以打断低优先级的业务，也可以打断预占、高优先级呼叫。
紧急报警功能包含哪四类业务？
紧急报警功能包括紧急呼叫、紧急告警、紧急鸣笛和报警发送GPS四类业务。
紧急报警业务的配置方式有哪些？
紧急报警业务可以单独配置（如“仅鸣笛”），也可以按照一定次序进行组合（如“紧急告警+紧急鸣笛”、“紧急告警+紧急呼叫”等）。
紧急呼叫功能采用什么过程发起，其优先级如何设定？
紧急呼叫功能采用紧急随机接入过程（C_Rand）发起紧急呼叫，呼叫优先级为“紧急”，其它过程和普通呼叫一致。
CSBKO 6 0111112 代表什么？
控制信令命令码
紧急呼叫在发射功率、呼叫记录以及未明确规定的处理流程上与普通呼叫有何异同？
紧急呼叫过程和普通呼叫过程一致，文档中未涉及到的过程均和普通呼叫同样处理。紧急呼叫默认使用高功率发射，通话结束后切换回原来的功率。紧急呼叫产生的呼叫记录与普通呼叫的呼叫记录一致，无特殊区分。
当终端被P_CLEAR信令从业务信道清除到控制信道后，在设定的一段时间内会处于什么状态？该状态下终端对非紧急业务的响应行为有哪些限制？
终端将处于“仅接收紧急语音个呼”状态。在此状态下：1. 界面无提示；2. 不响应终端发起的新业务；3. 不响应来自控制信道的非紧急语音个呼业务（包括数据业务、迟后信令、遥毙、遥晕、紧急警报、紧急组呼等）；4. 允许重新登记，且“仅接收紧急个呼”计时器正常计时。
当紧急报警目的ID设置为个呼时，在定时器内对呼叫的发起和接收有哪些限制？
只能发起对此ID的个呼，且只能接收此ID发过来的个呼，同时会拒绝此ID的组呼。
如果紧急报警目的ID被配置为组呼，在定时器期间系统允许进行哪些呼叫操作？
只能发起对此组ID的呼叫，且只能接收此组ID的呼叫。
在紧急报警目的ID设为个呼的情况下，定时器内是否会接受来自该ID的组呼请求？
不会，系统会拒绝此ID的组呼。
当终端向组呼告警且定时器未超时，此时收到该组的呼叫，能否接收此组呼呼叫？
可以接收此组呼呼叫，不论告警发起方的组呼旋钮在任何位置。
不同的报警模式下，声光示警的触发时机有何不同？
若报警模式为紧急呼叫，则在紧急呼叫结束后，发起声光示警。若报警模式为紧急警报，则不能发起声光示警。若报警模式为警报呼叫，则终端将在紧急警报及紧急呼叫结束后，发起声光示警。
在警报鸣笛的等待回呼时间内收到回呼，应如何处理后续流程？
在等待回呼时间内，如果收到回呼，需等呼叫结束后再启动鸣笛过程。
在警报呼叫的紧急警报阶段按下PTT键会产生什么影响？
在紧急警报阶段，如果按下PTT键，将直接进入非自动的紧急呼叫阶段；如果设置了Call To Follow，PTT会终止自动紧急呼叫流程。
通过报警键、倒放、单独工作或Foot Emergency方式发起紧急警报和呼叫时，报警号码应如何配置？
报警号码需要在CPS或MDM中设置，支持发送给当前联系人或指定号码。其中，“当前联系”指待机界面显示的组呼、个呼和全呼联系人；“指定号码”指“Emergency Number”参数中设置的号码。
如何使用【智能】旋钮切换信道或联系人，以及如何返回音量调节状态？
按下【智能】旋钮，旋转旋钮可以切换信道/联系人。如果5秒内未操作或在5秒内再次按下【智能】旋钮，将返回音量调节状态。
在数字集群模式下，使用“联系人/信道上调”和“联系人/信道下调”按键分别如何切换联系人？
在数字集群模式下，“联系人/信道上调”按照递增顺序切换组群中的组呼/个呼联系人；“联系人/信道下调”按照递减顺序切换组群中的组呼/个呼联系人。
常规模式下进行一键呼叫业务时，如何发起组呼？
需在按【一键呼叫/消息】快捷键后再按【PTT】键发起呼叫。
接收到个呼后，如何在预设时间内建立呼叫？
如果您在预设时间内按【PTT】键，将建立呼叫。
超时禁发功能的触发条件、表现及恢复方法是什么？
当个呼、组呼、全呼或模拟呼叫时按住【PTT】键的持续时间超过预设单次发射时间（默认为 60 秒），对讲机将自动终止发射并发出警告音。松开【PTT】键可以停止警告音。如需再次通话，请在预设时间后再次按住【PTT】键发射。此功能默认开启。
如何设置对讲机对组呼通话中每个成员的讲话进行自动录音？
点击“对讲设置”，点击“会话式录音”，开启后即可自动对组呼通话中每个成员的讲话进行录音。
当对讲机频谱资源的收发频率间隔为固定值或无规律时，应分别采用哪种控制信道扫描方式？
当对讲机频谱资源的收发频率间隔为固定值时，应采用固定控制信道扫描；当对讲机频率无规律时，应采用灵活控制信道扫描。
TMO 的全称及其对应的中文含义是什么？
TMO 的全称是 Trunked Mode Operation，中文含义为集群模式。
什么是紧急报警？本方案提供了哪些紧急报警服务？
紧急报警是指出现紧急状况时，用户通过简单、快捷的方式向指定的目的方（如特定用户或组）传递险情信息以便得到援助。本方案提供紧急呼叫、紧急状态消息、紧急GPS消息等多种紧急报警服务，其中紧急呼叫是最主要也是最重要的服务。
在 DMO 模式下，紧急呼叫的发起方式如何配置？
在 DMO 下，可由 CPS 配置决定紧急呼叫是保留在 DMO 下发起还是切换到 TMO 下发起，同时支持配置切换到 TMO 后使用的紧急呼叫号码。
紧急呼叫在优先级和信道资源分配方面有什么特点？
紧急呼叫作为优先级最高呼叫，可打断其他优先级较低正在进行中的呼叫；在终端不能立即获得信道资源分配时也非常有效。
在紧急静默呼叫中，对紧急组附属、紧急轮询、紧急保护功能及呼叫优先级有哪些限制？
紧急静默呼叫中，不支持紧急组附属、紧急轮询、紧急保护功能，且紧急呼叫优先级必须为 15。
按【报警退出键】退出报警与其他退出方式（如基站拆线、紧急呼叫结束）在提示音方面有什么区别？
按【报警退出键】退出报警有提示音，其余方式（包括但不限于基站拆线、紧急呼叫结束）退出报警无提示音。
当“紧急呼叫类型”设置为“不启用”时，报警功能对紧急呼叫的支持情况如何？其余情况下呢？
当“紧急呼叫类型”是“不启用”时，报警中不支持紧急呼叫功能；其余情况下，报警均支持紧急呼叫。
当 Hot Mic 功能开启时，按下【PTT】键会产生什么效果？
Hot Mic 开启时，按【PTT】会引起 Hot Mic 功能关闭。
什么是紧急轮询？
紧急轮询是指终端建立紧急呼叫通信后，无需用户按【PTT】，终端周期发送语音的功能。
在CPS中应如何设置紧急呼叫优先级？
在CPS中，“紧急呼叫优先级”应选择“紧急优先级”。
什么是默认组切换重发？
默认组切换重发是指默认组切换时是否重新发起紧急呼叫。
在紧急轮询过程中，除了计数器超出设定次数自动退出外，还有哪些情况会导致退出紧急轮询或紧急呼叫流程？
以下情况可导致退出：1. 轮询过程中发起方按下PTT，立即清除语音次数计数器，退出紧急轮询过程（但不退出紧急呼叫）；2. 终端或系统拆线，将退出紧急呼叫；3. 紧急呼叫时长超过基站或终端设置的普通呼叫通话时长，将退出紧急呼叫。
声光示警功能的触发条件、适用对象及表现形式有哪些规定？
声光示警仅对紧急报警发起方有效，对接收方无效。它只能通过紧急报警开启可编程键（包括倒放和单独工作）触发，单独发紧急状态消息不会触发。表现形式可设置为“鸣笛”或“鸣笛+闪光灯”。若配合GPS、紧急状态消息及紧急呼叫使用，将在这些流程结束后自动发起声光示警。
当配置为切换到集群模式发起紧急呼叫且采用集群模式紧急呼叫号码时，DMO 触发后的流程是怎样的？
DMO 触发紧急呼叫后，终端自动切换到 TMO 触发 TMO 下的紧急呼叫，发起的紧急呼叫类型取决于 TMO 紧急呼叫配置；呼叫结束，终端停留在 TMO 模式。
新的紧急呼叫号码采用什么类型的呼叫方式？
该号码类型为组呼，采用默认 COU 发起紧急组呼。
在 TMO 模式下基于新紧急号码发起的紧急呼叫取决于什么？
呼叫取决于 TMO 紧急组呼的相关配置。
在 TXI 模式下切换到集群模式时，如果 CPS 配置关闭了“切换模式时自动退出发射禁止”，用户选择“取消”后结果如何？
终端不退出发射禁止模式，并且不切换模式。
当紧急呼叫类型为“组呼”时，终端在报警期间对切组操作（如旋钮、快捷键）的响应策略是什么？
终端将默认组切到紧急组，然后整个报警期间不再响应切组操作（包括旋钮、快捷键等）。
终端在进行组呼业务时遇到紧急报警，会执行哪些操作？
触发报警、发送紧急状态消息，紧急呼叫阶段视报警配置及具体场景而定。
What is the title of TR 102 300-2?
Radio channels, network protocols and service performance
Which document covers Direct Mode Operation (DMO)?
What frequency range is covered by the new simulations for TETRA equipment performance requirements?
138 MHz to 300 MHz
What metrics are used to characterize the performance of TETRA V+D radio channels?
The performance of TETRA V+D radio channels is characterized in terms of Bit Error Ratio (BER) and Message Erasure Rate (MER).
Which two document identifiers refer to the same TETRA Voice plus Data Part 2 Air Interface document, and which one is used as the reference in this text?
ETSI EN 300 392-2 and ETSI TS 100 392-2 are two instances of the same document. Only ETSI EN 300 392-2 [i.2] is used as the reference in the present document for a shorter presentation.
What do the abbreviations AACH, BNCH, and BSCH stand for?
AACH stands for Access Assign CHannel, BNCH stands for Broadcast Network CHannel, and BSCH stands for Broadcast Synchronization CHannel.
Define the abbreviations DMO, C/Ic, and Es/N0 as used in this document.
DMO stands for Direct Mode Operation, C/Ic stands for Carrier on co-channel Interference ratio, and Es/N0 stands for Signal on Noise ratio.
What does the abbreviation SCH/HD stand for?
SCH/HD stands for Signalling CHannel, Half size Downlink.
How is TCH/x N=y defined in the context of traffic channels?
TCH/x N=y is defined as Traffic CHannel for x kbit/s and interleaving depth N=y.
How is performance measured for the TCH/S channel compared to other traffic channels?

For most traffic channels, performance is measured in terms of BER. However, due to the specific design of the TCH/S channel, its performance is measured in terms of both MER and residual BER (the BER detected on speech frames that are not discarded).
Under what condition is a speech frame discarded in the TCH/S channel?
A speech frame in the TCH/S channel is discarded if it is corrupted, specifically before entering the speech decoder.
Which logical channels support uplink, discontinuous downlink, and continuous downlink transmission modes?
Traffic channels and the SCH/F channel support all these transmission modes: uplink, discontinuous downlink, and continuous downlink.
Which receiver blocks are described as the mirror counterpart of transmitter blocks?
The receiver blocks that are the mirror counterpart of transmitter blocks are the root raised cosine filter, demodulator, differential decoder, burst splitter, de-scrambler and de-interleaver.
What carrier frequency was used in the simulations?
400 MHz carrier frequency.
How many MAC blocks were evaluated for each simulated point?
Each simulated point has been evaluated on a set of 10 000 MAC blocks.
What are the two groups of performance reported for each logical channel when available?
One group is for ideal synchronization technique, and the other is for realistic technique.
Which propagation environments are associated with Figure 2 for the MER of AACH with ideal synchronization?
TU50, BU50, RA200, and HT200.
What is the designed purpose of traffic channels?
Traffic channels are devoted to the transport of user information on the air interface when a short and constant delay is required by the service in action.
Which logical channel has been designed for the transport of coded speech?
The logical channel TCH/7,2 has been designed for the transport of the coded speech.
Which propagation environments are analyzed for the BER of TCH/7,2 with realistic synchronization technique in Figure 30?
The propagation environments analyzed are TU50, BU50, RA50, RA200, HT50, and HT200.
Which propagation environments are analyzed for the BER of TCH/4,8 with N=8 in Figure 44?
The propagation environments analyzed are TU5, TU50, and TU100.
What is the definition of a traffic scenario in the context of TETRA network performance evaluation?
A traffic scenario is the description of the traffic offered to the network by all the subscribers.
Which two types of users are generally identified for a TETRA network?
The two kinds of users generally identified for a TETRA network are public (PAMR) and private (PMR) network users.
What spatial distributions are commonly considered for user distribution in TETRA traffic scenarios?
User spatial distribution is commonly considered uniform or Gaussian. The Gaussian distribution is used when a town or people concentration is included in the area covered by the network.
How many physical channels can a radio link consist of at one time in a TETRA network?
The radio link consists of one to four physical channels at time.
How can the LLC layer optimize the transmission of layer 3 messages for the same subscriber?
The LLC layer can put layer 3 messages for the same subscriber on a single LLC PDU (BL-DATA and BL-ACK) until the reception of a MAC_READY signal from the MAC layer.
How does the MAC layer determine when data are ready for transmission by the LLC layer?
The MAC layer knows when data are ready to be transmitted by the LLC through the DATA IN BUFFER PDU.
What capability does the MAC layer have regarding LLC messages and timeslots?
The MAC layer can fit more than one LLC message on a single timeslot.
What is the TDMA frame duration specified in the time diagrams?
The TDMA frame duration is 56.67 ms.
What is the role of the MLE layer in relation to layers 2 and 3?
The MLE layer is considered a transparent entity devoted to route primitives between layers 2 and 3.
How does connectionless data transmission work in a TETRA network?

In connectionless transmission, the packet is sent to the network without any negotiation with the called party. Each network node routes the packet to adjacent nodes up to the called party using the complete called party address.
What are the requirements for connection-oriented data transmission in a TETRA network?

A virtual connection with the called party must be set up before the first packet transmission. Subsequent transmissions use the same call identifier, and packets are routed through this connection identifier, which is shorter than the complete address.
What are the two types of links offered by LLC in TETRA standard documents, and how do they differ in availability?
LLC offers Basic link and Advanced link. The Basic link is always available in the LLC, whereas the Advanced link requires a set up phase.
What is the difference in traffic channel allocation between message trunking systems and transmission trunking systems?

In message trunking systems, traffic channels are allocated for the lifetime of the call. In transmission trunking systems, channel allocation is limited to an 'over', after which the call must obtain the radio resource again.
Does the TETRA standard define Dispatcher applications or operations?
No, the TETRA standard does not describe Dispatcher applications or operations.
What metrics are used to report the performance of a logical channel in relation to Es/N0 or C/Ic?
The performance is given as MER or BER.
What is the assumed relationship between static Es/N0 on the MS and BS sides during a MAC block transmission?
The static Es/N0, which does not take into account fading and shadowing processes, is assumed to be equal on both the Mobile Station (MS) and Base Station (BS) sides during a MAC block transmission.
How does the open loop power control process on the MS function and what threshold was used in actual simulations?

The open loop power control on the MS operates based on the received radio signal from the BS, where the measured power level is an average of signal samples that filters out fading effects. A power control threshold is fixed to reduce transmitted power when the estimated signal received by the BS exceeds it. In actual simulations, a threshold of 22 dBs was considered, corresponding to a 5 dB margin over the reference sensitivity.
What are the two specific cases that cause co-channel interference (Ic) in TETRA systems?
Co-channel interference (Ic) is caused by: 1) signals coming from external cells when frequency reuse algorithms are adopted, and 2) simultaneous random access attempts.
How can co-channel interference (Ic) be evaluated if the position and speed of interference generators are known?

If the position and speed of interference generators are known, Ic can be evaluated as the sum of power levels received from each generator, using the formula for the evaluation of the wanted signal power.
What mechanism reduces adjacent channel interference (Iad) power before the signal enters the receiver, and how is the remaining portion determined?

Input filters in the receiver reduce the interference power before signal entrance. The portion of the signal power of adjacent channel transmissions is given as a function of the Net Filter Discrimination.
How can suitable values for channel performance be obtained when relating signal-to-overall-noise ratio to channel figures?
Suitable values for channel performance can be obtained by matching the evaluated signal-to-overall-noise ratio with channel figures as functions of Es/N0.
What are the possible outcomes when simultaneous transmissions occur on the random access channel?
There are cases where one colliding signal is correctly decoded by the BS; otherwise, the collision is totally destructive.
How does the MCCH structure adapt to different traffic loads?
When the total amount of traffic is low, a single control channel can be employed as MCCH. In case of high loads, the MCCH can be supplemented by an additional control channel.
What is the reference value for the Random access Back off time (WT) in Table 8?
The reference value for the Random access Back off time (WT) is 5 TDMA frames.
How are Access Codes allocated on the Control Channel in this scenario?
What is the relationship between control channel capacity and short data transmission frequency?
The control channel capacity decreases when the short data transmission frequency increases.
What is studied in case of a MCCH that consists of two control channels?
the possibility of splitting the total amount of traffic depending on the traffic type
Under what conditions is the difference in delay performance between discrete and rolling access frames more evident?
The difference is more evident when access opportunities are few due to a high number of reserved slots, which corresponds to high traffic loads.
What is the average waiting time for an accessing MS in the case of discrete access frames?
In the case of discrete access frames, the average waiting time is equal to half of an access frame duration.
What is the duplex mode for a group voice call from a Dispatcher to a group of TETRA MSs?
Half duplex.
What is the primary purpose of the analysis regarding allocated traffic channels?
The analysis is done in order to give an estimate of the degradation of performance when the number of allocated traffic channels becomes low.
What are the time threshold values for the reference scenario and the compared configuration regarding maximum hold time in priority queues?
The reference scenario uses a time threshold of 100 TDMA frames, while the compared configuration uses a time threshold of 300 TDMA frames.
What method is used to obtain a reliable estimate of BER given its time variability?
To have a reliable estimate, the evaluated performance is usually expressed as a probability function, which allows evaluating statistic boundaries of the BER in simulated environments.
What operating frequency is always assumed for the reference traffic scenarios in TETRA V+D networks?
An operating frequency of 400 MHz is always assumed.
How is the position of subscribers described in the context of TETRA network traffic scenarios?
The position of subscribers is described in terms of the probability to be located in a particular point on the covered area.
What is the basis for the group call set-up procedure in a TETRA V+D network?
The procedure is based on EN 300 392-2 [i.2], annex D.
What happens during MS originated transmission after random access?
After random access, a suitable amount of uplink timeslots are reserved for the remaining bytes, and the acknowledgement is sent back by the SwMI at the end of the last transmitted slot.
Describe the sequence of events for MS terminated transmission.

The SwMI pages the MS and waits for the MS acknowledgement; then, a sequence of downlink slots are reserved for the remaining part of transmission. After the last slot, the MS sends the acknowledgement of the whole packet.
How does the SwMI handle channel assignment in all cases described?

A late channel assignment is performed: after the paging procedure, the availability of channels is checked, and then the Connection procedure is performed or delayed depending on the call management strategy.
What frequency range does the TETRA standard EN 300 392-2 address?
The TETRA standard EN 300 392-2 addresses frequencies between 300 MHz and 1 GHz.
At what frequency were the TETRA Protocol stack design and simulation results for π/4-DQPSK originally conducted in EN 300 392-2?
The TETRA Protocol stack design and simulation results for π/4-DQPSK shown in EN 300 392-2 were conducted for 400 MHz.
Which clauses present the performance of logical channels over TU50 and HT200 propagation channels respectively?
The performance of logical channels over the TU50 propagation channel is presented in clause F.2.2, while the performance over the HT200 propagation channel is presented in clause F.2.3.
What are the Doppler shift values for TU50 and HT200 propagation channels at 430 MHz?
At 430 MHz, the Doppler shift is 20 Hz for the TU50 propagation channel and 80 Hz for the HT200 propagation channel.
How does the Doppler spread effect on slot count compare between 138 MHz and 430 MHz for TU50 and HT200 channels?
For the TU50 channel, Doppler spread affects 12 slots at 138 MHz compared to 4 slots at 430 MHz. For the HT200 channel, Doppler spread affects 3 slots at 138 MHz compared to 1 slot at 430 MHz.
What performance metric is used to characterize AACH, BSCH, SCH/F, and SCH/HU logical channels?
The performance characteristics for AACH, BSCH, SCH/F, and SCH/HU logical channels are given as message error rate (MER).
Which propagation environments are used for the BER plots of TCH/7,2, TCH/2,4, and TCH/4,8 logical channels?
The BER plots for these logical channels are provided over TU50 and HT200 propagation environments.
What is the channel encoding method and bit configuration for AACH?
AACH is a Reed Muller encoded channel with only 14 type-1 bits.
How does the performance of SCH/F over the TU50 channel at 138 MHz compare to its performance at 430 MHz?
The performance of SCH/F over the TU50 channel at 138 MHz is about 4 dB worse than the performance of the same system over 430 MHz at 10e-3.
Why is the performance of SCH/F over the TU5 channel at 430 MHz considered the worst?
It is worst due to less Doppler shift, which consequently affects more slots and results in a higher Message Error Rate (MER).
What are the design specifications and performance characteristics of the SCH/HU logical channel?

SCH/HU is designed as RCPC encoded with a rate of 2/3 and 92 type-1 bits. Its performance over TU50 at 138 MHz is about 4 dB worse than at 430 MHz. Additionally, its performance over TU5 at 430 MHz is 6 dB to 7 dB worse.
What is the channel encoding and bit configuration for TCH/7,2?
TCH/7,2 is an un-coded channel with 432 type-1 bits.
Why does TCH/7,2 over the TU50 channel at 138 MHz perform slightly better in terms of BER compared to other conditions?
It performs slightly better due to reduced Doppler shift over the un-coded channel.
How does the performance of TCH/2,4 over the TU5 channel at 430 MHz compare to its performance over the TU50 channel at 10e-3 BER?
The performance over the TU5 channel at 430 MHz is worse than over the TU50 channel by around 10 dB at 10e-3.
What is the encoding rate and bit configuration for the TCH/2,4 channel?
The TCH/2,4 channel is RCPC encoded with a rate of 148/432 and contains 144 type-1 bits.
How does interleaving over 4 blocks affect the system performance of the TCH/2,4 channel?
Interleaving over 4 blocks improves the system performance.
Why does the TCH/2,4 channel experience a loss of performance in the TU50 channel at 138 MHz compared to a similar operating environment at 430 MHz?
The Doppler spread over the 138 MHz TU50 channel extends over 11 timeslots, resulting in a loss of performance compared to the similar operating environment over 430 MHz.
What is the performance difference of the TCH/2,4 logical channel over TU50 at 138 MHz at a BER of 10e-3?
The performance of the logical channel over TU50 at 138 MHz is out by 5 dB at 10e-3.
What is the channel encoding rate and number of type-1 bits for the TCH/2,4 logical channel?
The TCH/2,4 channel uses RCPC encoding with a rate of 148/432 and contains 144 type-1 bits.
How does interleaving over 8 blocks affect the BER performance of TCH/2,4 over the TU50 channel at 138 MHz?
Interleaving over 8 blocks reduces the BER performance requirement by 6 dB at 10e-3 for TCH/2,4 over the TU50 channel at 138 MHz.
How does the performance of TCH/2,4 N=8 over the TU5 channel at 430 MHz compare to its performance over the TU50 channel?
The performance of TCH/2,4 N=8 over the TU5 channel at 430 MHz is worse than over the TU50 channel by around 22 dB at 10e-3.
What is the encoding rate and number of type-1 bits for the TCH/4,8 channel?
The TCH/4,8 channel is RCPC encoded with a rate of 292/432 and 288 type-1 bits.
How does the BER performance of TCH/4,8 with interleaving over 4 blocks for TU50 channel at 138 MHz compare to that at 430 MHz?
The BER performance of TCH/4,8 with interleaving over 4 blocks for TU50 channel over 138 MHz is 4 to 5 dB worse at 10e-3 compared to the performance at TU50 channel over 430 MHz.
What is the performance difference of TCH/4,8 N=4 over TU5 channel at 430 MHz compared to TU50 at a BER of 10e-3?
The performance of TCH/4,8 N=4 over TU5 channel at 430 MHz is worse than that at TU50 by around 14 dB at 10e-3.
How many type-1 bits does the AACH channel have?
AACH is a Reed Muller encoded channel with only 14 type-1 bits.
What are the design specifications for the SCH/F channel associated with Figure F.18?
SCH/F is designed as RCPC encoded with a rate of 2/3 and utilizes 268 type-1 bits.
Why is the performance of SCH/F over the HT50 channel at 430 MHz considered worse?
The performance is worse due to less Doppler shift, which results in effects on more slots and consequently affects the Message Error Rate (MER).
Which propagation environment and frequency are depicted in Figure F.17 for the BSCH channel?
Figure F.17 shows the Message Error Rate of BSCH over the HT200 Propagation Channel for 138 MHz.
Why is the performance of SCH/HU over the HT50 channel at 430 MHz considered the worst?
It is the worst due to less Doppler shift, which results in effects on more slots and consequently affects the Message Error Rate (MER).
What are the characteristics of the TCH/7,2 logical channel described in the text?
TCH/7,2 is an un-coded channel with 432 type-1 bits.
What is the coding rate and number of type-1 bits for the TCH/2,4 RCPC encoded channel?
The TCH/2,4 RCPC encoded channel has a rate of 148/432 with 144 type-1 bits.
How does interleaving over 8 blocks affect the system performance of the TCH/2,4 channel?
Interleaving over 8 blocks improves the system performance.
What causes the loss of performance for the TCH/2,4 channel at 138 MHz in an HT200 channel compared to a similar environment at 430 MHz?
The Doppler shift over 138 MHz at the HT200 channel is spread over 3 timeslots, resulting in a loss of performance compared with a similar operating environment over 430 MHz.
How much worse is the BER performance of TCH/2,4 with interleaving over 8 blocks for the HT200 channel over 138 MHz at a BER of 10e-4?
The BER performance is worse by 2 dB at 10e-4.
What is the encoding type, rate, and number of type-1 bits for the TCH/4,8 channel?
TCH/4,8 is an RCPC encoded channel with a rate of 292/432 and 288 type-1 bits.
How does the BER performance of TCH/4,8 over the HT200 channel at 138 MHz compare to that at 430 MHz?
The performance of TCH/4,8 over the HT200 channel at 138 MHz is worse than at HT200 at 430 MHz.
Why does the TCH/4,8 channel at 138 MHz over HT200 experience a loss of performance compared to the similar operating environment over 430 MHz?
At 138 MHz over the HT200 channel, TCH/4,8 is spread over 3 timeslots, resulting in a loss of performance compared with the similar operating environment over 430 MHz.
How does interleaving differ between the N=4 and N=8 cases for TCH/2,4 and TCH/4,8 logical channels?
In the N=4 case for TCH/2,4 and TCH/4,8, interleaving is carried over the 4 blocks rather than within the block. In the N=8 case, interleaving is carried over the 8 blocks and also within the block.
Which specific logical channels are simulated for 430 MHz and 138 MHz frequencies?
The logical channels simulated for 430 MHz and 138 MHz are AACH, BSCH, SCH/F, SCH/HU, TCH/7,2, TCH/4,8, and TCH/2,4.
What components of the simulation system are based on clauses 4.2, 5, and 6.6.3 of EN 300 392-2 [i.2]?
